The Component Reference

26-agent audit

ELEMENTS
●  paragraph
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable — a paragraph is native contenteditable prose, every inline mark included, insertable via slash and Enter.
The most elemental block — meaning with nothing but its own text.
Code: canvas/index.js:540-558, :557, :580-583, :807-810, :832-834; slash-insert.js:40; bp-attrs.js:30,38
●  heading
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas: type the text inline, change the level via Cmd-P or Markdown — and it's slash-insertable.
A titled break, levels 1–6.
Fix:
Add a visible level control (dropdown or bubble button) on the heading block so changing level is discoverable.
Code: run-convert.js:541-542, index.js:568-569 & :971-998, command-palette.js:267-269, slash-insert.js:94
●  list
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas: item text and bullet/ordered are both real, and it's slash-insertable.
Ordered or bulleted list; nestable.
Fix:
Add a bullet/ordered toggle to the format bubble and an ordered-list slash entry.
Code: command-palette.js:270-271, convert.js:406-413, slash-insert.js:42,97-103, slash-menu.js:22, format-bubble.js
◐  eyebrow
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Fully editable text if it already exists, but you can't create an eyebrow from the canvas.
A kicker label above a title.
Fix:
Add eyebrow to CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES; its "no node-view" exclusion reason is now stale.
Code: role-nodes.js:67-90 (:70 marks, :87 hole), run-convert.js:96, slash-insert.js:35, canvas/index.js:378-379,:1534, command-palette.js:59
◐  byline
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Barely editable: you can retype the one authors line, but the "list" is fake middot-text — no add/remove, no marks, no insert.
An author / credit line.
Fix:
Add per-author fields with add/remove controls, allow link marks, and list byline in CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES.
Code: role-nodes.js:95-99, run-convert.js:1738-1749, slash-insert.js:34-62
◐  ingress
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas — click into the lede and type like a paragraph, marks and all; you just can't slash-insert one.
The lede / standfirst paragraph.
Fix:
Add ingress to CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES so the slash menu can insert a lede in-canvas.
Code: role-nodes.js:131,120-122; canvas/index.js:722,378-379,1534; slash-insert.js:34-62; paper_editor.ex:656,631-649; handlers/paper.ex:291-319
◐  pullquote
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Quote text is fully editable inline with marks, but you can't insert a new pullquote from the canvas.
A large pulled quote.
Fix:
Add pullquote to CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES so it appears in the slash menu and can be inserted.
Code: role-nodes.js:152-175,:30-35; slash-insert.js:34-62; index.js:378,:1534; slash-menu.js:33; run-convert.js:99; __role.test.mjs:107
●  divider
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully handled: an empty-payload atom with nothing to author — you insert it and delete it, that's the whole surface.
A section rule (§) — no payload.
Code: slash-insert.js:46,:117-118; divider-node.js:49,:61,:68,:100; figures.ex:33-37
●  code
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable: code body is a real textarea, language a real input, and it inserts from the slash menu.
A fenced code block with a language.
Code: code-node.js:224-231, :236-249, :261-271, :280, :337, :344; slash-insert.js:45, :115-116; Figures.code_block_html:221-223
●  diagram
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable — both Mermaid source and caption are real in-canvas controls and it's slash-insertable, but you edit raw code blind.
A Mermaid diagram + caption.
Fix:
Add an inline rendered Mermaid preview beside the source textarea and always-show the caption field.
Code: diagram-node.js:235-246, :258-265, :277-289, :342-376; slash-insert.js:47,119-120; blocks.ex:238
●  action
FULL
· element · insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas: label, href, and priority each have a live native control, and the block is slash-insertable.
A CTA button / link.
Code: action-node.js:223-249, :261-282, :303-319, :333-335, :272-274; template-lock :153-164
◐  image
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Barely — a pre-seeded featured slot where you can only swap the picture; nothing else is typed.
A content image (src + alt).
Fix:
Add an alt-text input, expose role, and register image in CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES so it can be inserted.
Code: paper_editor.ex:1280-1289,1331-1336; root.html.heex:2949-2976,5080-5102; bp-media-picker.js:560,584,601,639; slash-insert.js:37-62
◐  field-* (native ×7)
PARTIAL
· element · insertable.
All 7 native field types insert and their value edits live in-canvas — but label, schema binding, and select options stay read-only config.
Schema-bound field controls.
Fix:
Add in-canvas controls for label, fieldName binding, and select-option editing to make the whole field authorable.
Code: field-node.js:907-972 (buildControl), :527/:560 (label), :338-345 (fieldName), :571-604 (patch); slash-insert.js:55-61,161-176; paper_editor.ex:939
◐  field-image / field-reference
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Narrowly editable — you can set the asset or linked doc in-canvas, but nothing else and you can't even insert one.
Media + reference picker fields.
Fix:
Add field-image/field-reference to CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES and expose label/refType/dataset as canvas controls.
Code: field-node.js:245-281, :674-676, :711, :743-776, :797-847; run-convert.js:245-249, :2113-2116; slash-insert.js:37-62; canvas/index.js:378-379, :1534-1535
◐  composite / arrayOf / codelist / localizedText
PARTIAL
· element · not insertable.
Values of all four composite types are fully editable in the side rail — but you can't insert one, there's no in-canvas editing, and the shape is JSON-only.
Nested schema field structures.
Fix:
Add canvas node-views + slash-insert entries for all four, plus UI to edit field shape instead of raw JSON.
Code: paper_field_block.ex:271-320, :399-504, :253-261; composite_field.ex:204-328; array_field.ex:278-331; localized_text_field.ex:110-126; slash-insert.js:32-62; paper_editor.ex:1301
WIDGETS
◐  callout
PARTIAL
· widget · insertable.
Only the body prose is truly canvas-editable — title is inert chrome and tone is set once at birth.
A toned box + title + body.
Fix:
Add an in-canvas tone picker and an editable title input to the callout node-view.
Code: callout-node.js:264,272-291,301-336,345; index.js:1459,1462; slash-insert.js:31
●  table
FULL
· widget · insertable.
Genuinely full: cells are real contenteditable inline holes and rows, cols, and header are live buttons.
A grid of cells with an optional header row.
Fix:
Add interior insert/delete and drag-reorder for rows and columns to make blunt editing precise.
Code: table-node.js:290-415 (renderHTML/buttons), TRANSFORMS:136-158, run-convert.js:1626-1633/1693-1699, slash-insert.js:53/147-155
◐  card
PARTIAL
· widget · not insertable.
Only title and body edit in-canvas (body silently drops formatting); media/action are raw-string inputs, tone unexposed, card not insertable.
A composed widget: title + body + media/action slots.
Fix:
Add a tone control, media picker with alt, action-priority field, preserve body marks, and register a slash-menu insert.
Code: card-node.js:159,178-196,199-219,247-260,304-371; slots.ex:280-286
●  note
FULL
· widget · insertable.
Fully editable in-canvas: body text plus label and lead inputs all live-edit, and it's slash-insertable.
An annotated item: label + lead + body.
Code: note-node.js:58,138-158,215-246,254; islands :164-179; PM-hidden :261-272; lossy note :34-36
●  stage
FULL
· widget · insertable.
Fully editable: all five authored fields are live native controls that write back, and it inserts from the slash menu.
A pipeline-node twin: kind/title/detail.
Code: stage-node.js:172-186, :228-244, :257-261, :92-105; slash-insert.js:54, :156-160
◐  terminal
PARTIAL
· widget · insertable.
Chrome and prose command-lines edit inline, but any non-prose child becomes a read-only JSON chip.
Terminal chrome wrapping child blocks.
Fix:
Give non-prose children real in-canvas node-views instead of the verbatim JSON carrier chip.
Code: terminal-node.js:192-263 (chrome), :298 & :60-63 (prose body), :402/:417/:418 (chip); slash-insert.js:52, :143-146
◐  figure
PARTIAL
· widget · insertable.
Barely — you can edit the caption and nothing else; the figure's actual content is a read-only server-painted atom.
A single child block + a caption.
Fix:
Add an in-canvas child editor — image picker/upload plus a swap control — so the figure body is authorable.
Code: figure-node.js:200-224, :291-317, :114-136, :76,281-286, :177,339-342; slash-insert.js:77-78,123-128
◐  task-list
PARTIAL
· widget · not insertable.
Title and query-label edit live with server-bound rows, but you can't insert it and every other facet is raw-JSON only.
A live task query, rows resolved at read.
Fix:
Add facet + config controls (project/status/parent selects, limit/fields select) and register it in CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES.
Code: task-list-node.js:222-236, :329-384, :42-82, :153-155, :245-289; slash-insert.js:39-62
○  fleet · the read-only ten
VIEW-ONLY
· widget · not insertable.
View-only: all ten atoms are server-painted and read-only — the canvas can select and delete them, but edit nothing.
tasks · task-detail · task-board · roadmap · status-legend · asciicast · form · questionnaire · sheet · embed.
Fix:
Add real node-view controls (fields/inputs) per kind and register the types in CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES.
Code: embed-node.js:162-167, :400-415, :22-27,101-116,240-267, :457-523; paper_canvas.ex:167; slash-insert.js:32,39-62
SECTIONS & LAYOUT
◐  section
PARTIAL
· section · insertable.
Name it, edit its blocks, flip stack⇄grid, set column count — but per-child span/order, gap, and breakpoints stay raw-JSON.
A layout container: title + children + layout spec.
Fix:
Add a per-child span/order picker (or drag-resize) plus gap and breakpoint controls that write layout attrs.
Code: section-node.js:280-320 (title/mode/tracks), :335-372 cells paint, :73-79 gap; slash-insert.js:51,:133-142
◐  columns
PARTIAL
· section · insertable.
Prose inside columns is fully editable, but you can't add/remove columns or edit rich children — a column filler, not a builder.
A multi-column layout.
Fix:
Add canvas add/remove-column controls and let non-prose children render editable instead of read-only chips.
Code: columns-node.js:138-141, :50/:129 (slash), :74-92 (static cols), :157-198/:249-273 (atom chip), :242 (delete)

Choosing Your Site Framework
You're about to
spawn a site
on Barkpark Cloud — a live frontend that reads straight from your content. This guide exists so you can make that choice with open eyes: what each framework is genuinely good at, where it will bite you, and which one fits the site you actually want to ship. There is no single right answer — only the right answer *for your project*.
The short version.
For most content sites — blogs, docs, marketing, portfolios —
Astro
is the best default, and it's the one you can spawn today. If you need a heavily interactive app, you'll want a server-rendered framework like Next.js or TanStack Start. Read on for why.
First, the decision that matters most
Before the framework, understand the axis every framework sits on. It decides your site's speed, cost, and how much can go wrong.
What it is
Every page is built once into plain HTML/CSS/JS
Pages are assembled by a live server on each request
Speed
Fastest possible — files served from the edge
Fast, but every request does work
Cost & scale
Effectively free, scales infinitely
Costs grow with traffic; needs a running process
Best for
Content that changes on a human schedule
Content that's personalised or changes per-request
What can break
Almost nothing at runtime
The server, under load or on bad input
Barkpark keeps your
site and your content on the same wire
— the site fetches from your Barkpark project over an internal connection, not the public internet. That means faster builds, private reads, and instant updates when your content changes. Static sites get this at build time; server-rendered sites get it on every request.
Why "close" matters here
Instant content updates
— when you publish in Barkpark, your site knows immediately (no manual redeploy).
No rate limits, no egress fees
— your site reads content over a private link, not a metered public API.
One login, one domain, one dashboard
— the site inherits your workspace, project, and dataset scoping.
One deploy pipeline
— updates roll out with zero downtime, the same way the rest of your Barkpark runs.
The frameworks at a glance
Astro
JS / TS
Content sites
Static or SSR
Almost none
Available now
Next.js
JS / TS
Everything
Static or SSR
A lot

TanStack Start

Interactive apps

JS / TS

Static or SSR

JS / TS (Vue)
Content + app

None
Available now
"Ships JS by default"
is a proxy for page weight and speed. Less shipped JavaScript means faster loads and better search rankings — which is why content-first frameworks win on SEO.
The frameworks in depth
Astro — the content-site flagship
Astro is built for exactly what a CMS produces: pages of content. It renders to static HTML by default and only ships JavaScript for the interactive "islands" you explicitly ask for. If you're building a blog, documentation site, marketing site, or portfolio, this is the one to reach for.
Best for:
blogs, docs, marketing sites, portfolios, landing pages, changelogs.
Pros
Blazing fast by design
— ships near-zero JavaScript, so pages load instantly and score top marks on Core Web Vitals.
Built for headless CMS
— its content layer is designed to pull from an external source like Barkpark, so the integration is natural, not bolted on.
Excellent SEO out of the box
— fast, static, semantic HTML is what search engines reward.
Use any UI library
— drop in React, Svelte, Vue, or Solid components as islands; you're not locked into one.
Gentle learning curve
— if you know HTML and a little JS, you can be productive in an afternoon.
Cheapest to host
— static output means your site is basically free to serve and scales without limit.
Grows with you
— start static, add server-rendering later for the few pages that need it.
Huge, active ecosystem
of themes and integrations to start from.
Cons
Not built for app-like UIs
— if your site is mostly dashboards, live filtering, or complex client state, Astro's island model fights you.
Islands take a mental shift
— sharing state between separate interactive components is deliberately awkward.
Smaller component ecosystem
than the React/Next world.
Server-rendering is younger
than Next's — battle-tested less at very large scale.
Recommended default, and spawnable today.
If you're unsure, start here — you can always graduate to a heavier framework later.
Next.js — the do-everything heavyweight
Next.js is the most popular React framework and can build essentially any kind of site — from a static blog to a full SaaS app. That power comes with weight and complexity.
Best for:
apps with logged-in users, dashboards, e-commerce, anything that mixes content with heavy interactivity.
Pros
Does everything
— static pages, server-rendering, and incremental updates all in one framework.
The largest ecosystem
— the most tutorials, templates, integrations, and hireable developers of any framework here.
Great for interactive apps
— if your site has accounts, carts, or dashboards, Next is at home.
Incremental Static Regeneration
— pages can rebuild in the background as content changes, blending static speed with fresh data.
First-class React
— access to the entire React component universe.
Cons
Heavy
— ships a lot of JavaScript, so pages are slower than a static Astro or Hugo site unless carefully tuned.
Complex
— React Server Components and the App Router have a real learning curve, and the "right way" keeps evolving.
Frequent breaking changes
— major versions can mean real migration work.
Server-rendering costs more to run
— dynamic pages need a live process, which grows with traffic.
Overkill for a brochure site
— you'll carry complexity you never use.
TanStack Start — the modern, type-safe challenger
TanStack Start is a newer full-stack React framework built around the excellent TanStack Router. It prioritises end-to-end type safety and a fast, modern developer experience.
Best for:
highly interactive, data-heavy applications where type safety and routing power matter.
Pros
End-to-end type safety
— from your routes to your data, mistakes get caught before they ship.
Best-in-class routing
— TanStack Router handles complex, nested, data-driven navigation elegantly.
Fast, modern tooling
— built on Vite, so builds and hot-reload are quick.
Excellent for interactive apps
— streaming server-rendering keeps data-heavy pages snappy.
Cons
The newest option here
— smaller community, fewer templates, fewer answers when you hit a wall.
Not content-first
— overkill for a blog or marketing site.
Server-rendering runtime
— same running-process cost as Next.
Fewer hireable specialists
— a smaller talent pool than React/Next.
Younger = more risk
— APIs are still settling compared to mature frameworks.
SvelteKit — small, fast, and pleasant
SvelteKit compiles your components away at build time, so the browser downloads very little framework code. It handles both static and server-rendered sites and is widely loved for its developer experience.
Best for:
teams who want small, fast sites and enjoy a clean, minimal syntax — content or app.
Pros
Tiny bundles
— the framework compiles itself out, so pages are light and fast.
Loved developer experience
— concise syntax, less boilerplate than React.
Flexible
— does static and server-rendering equally well.
Built-in essentials
— routing, data loading, and forms come in the box.
Cons
Smaller ecosystem
than React — fewer ready-made components and integrations.
Fewer Svelte developers
to hire than React developers.
Server-rendering runtime cost
when you choose SSR.
Less enterprise track record
than Next at very large scale.
Nuxt — the Vue powerhouse
Nuxt is to Vue what Next is to React: a mature, full-featured framework for building both content sites and applications. If your team knows Vue, this is the natural home.
Best for:
Vue teams building content-rich sites or full applications.
Pros
Mature and complete
— years of production use, batteries included.
Great content tooling
— a dedicated content module makes CMS-driven sites straightforward.
Does static and server-rendering
— flexible per page.
Approachable
— Vue is often considered gentler to learn than React.
Cons
Smaller talent pool here
than React-based options.
Server-rendering runtime cost
identical to Next when you go SSR.
Ships more JS
than an islands or compiled framework like Astro or Svelte.
Vue-only
— you can't borrow the React component universe.
Hugo — the fastest static builder there is
Hugo is a single Go binary that turns content into a static site faster than anything else on this list. No Node.js, no runtime — just files. It's a superb fit for large content sites where build speed matters.
Best for:
large blogs, documentation, and content sites where raw build speed and simplicity win.
Pros
Fastest builds on the market
— thousands of pages in seconds.
No JavaScript runtime needed
— a single binary, nothing to keep alive, nothing to patch.
Cheapest and safest to host
— pure static output, no server code to attack.
Massive theme library
— hundreds of ready-made designs.
Rock-solid and stable
— mature, with few breaking changes.
Cons
Weak on interactivity
— no built-in "islands" story; dynamic bits need hand-rolled JavaScript.
Go templates are clunkier
than modern component syntax.
Not for app-like sites
— static only, by design.
Smaller front-end developer familiarity
than the JavaScript frameworks.
Eleventy (11ty) — dead-simple static
Eleventy is a minimalist static site generator. It does very little on purpose, which makes it fast, predictable, and easy to reason about.
Best for:
simple content sites where you want maximum control and minimum magic.
Pros
Extremely simple
— little to learn, little to go wrong.
Zero JavaScript shipped
— pages are as light as they get.
Fast builds
and a tiny footprint.
Template-language freedom
— write pages in whichever templating style you like.
Cons
No interactivity story
— you add all dynamic behaviour yourself.
Very hands-on
— the minimalism means more wiring for anything non-trivial.
Smaller ecosystem
than Astro or Next.
Static only
— no server-rendering path.
Barkpark Native — the instant, zero-effort site
Not every site needs a framework. Barkpark can render your content as a live site directly — no build step, no code, no framework to learn. Publish content, get a site. It's the fastest way from "I have content" to "it's online."
Best for:
getting content live in seconds, previews, and anyone who doesn't want to touch a framework at all.
Pros
Instant
— live in seconds, with nothing to build or deploy.
Zero code and zero maintenance
— Barkpark handles the rendering and the updates.
Always in sync
— the site *is* your content; there's no separate copy to fall out of date.
No runtime to pay for or secure
— it runs on infrastructure you already have.
Cons
Barkpark's look, not yours
— you theme within what Barkpark offers, rather than designing freely.
Not for bespoke designs
— if you need pixel-level custom layouts, reach for a framework.
Limited custom interactivity
— it's a content site, not an app platform.
Available today.
The zero-friction way to get online while you decide whether you need a full framework.
How to choose — by what you're building
A blog or newsletter
Astro
or
Barkpark Native
Content-first, fast, great SEO, minimal fuss
Documentation
Astro
or
Hugo
Fast static builds, easy navigation, huge page counts
A marketing / landing site
Astro
Fast, SEO-strong, easy to make beautiful
A portfolio
Astro
or
Barkpark Native
Looks great, ships fast, little to maintain
A site with logins / dashboards
Next.js
or
TanStack Start
Server-rendering handles per-user, interactive pages
An e-commerce store
Next.js
Mature ecosystem, handles carts, checkout, and scale
A huge documentation corpus
Hugo
Unbeatable build speed at thousands of pages
"I just want it online now"
Barkpark Native
Zero build, live in seconds
How your site goes live — and stays live
Every site you spawn deploys the same way, whether it's Astro, Hugo, or Barkpark Native. The process is built around one promise:
your live site never goes down, and a broken build never reaches your visitors.
1. Trigger
You click deploy — or you simply publish content and Barkpark rebuilds on its own
No manual redeploy for content changes
2. Build in isolation
Your site is built on separate infrastructure, reading your content over a private link
Your live site keeps serving the whole time
3. Health check
The new build is tested before anyone sees it
A broken build stops here — your current site is untouched
4. Atomic switch
The instant the new build passes, visitors flip to it
Zero downtime, no half-updated state
5. Instant rollback
The previous version is kept, ready to restore
If something's wrong, revert in one click, instantly
Publish-to-live.
Change content in Barkpark and your site updates automatically — no redeploy, no waiting, no broken pages in between.
Because your site is built and served
right next to your content
, deploys are fast and updates are near-instant. There's nothing to wire up: spawn the site, and this pipeline is simply how it works.
What you can spawn today — and what's coming
Barkpark Cloud rolls these out in order of demand. Every framework plugs into the same engine, so the ones marked *coming* are add-ons on a shared foundation, not rewrites.
Available now:
Astro (static) and Barkpark Native (instant).
Next up:
Hugo — proving the same engine serves a second static framework with zero Node runtime.
Then:
Next.js and TanStack Start — server-rendered frameworks, once the secure per-site runtime lands.
After that:
SvelteKit, Nuxt, and Eleventy — filling out the menu.
Escape hatch:
for teams who want a global edge or a fully managed host, Barkpark can also deploy your site to an external platform instead of running it close to your content.
Not sure? Start with Astro.
It covers the vast majority of sites beautifully, it's spawnable today, and nothing you build is wasted if you later graduate to a heavier framework.
*This guide is maintained by the Barkpark Cloud team. Framework capabilities and availability evolve — check your Cloud dashboard for the current menu when you spawn a site.*

Every site you spawn deploys the same way, whether it's Astro, Hugo, or Barkpark Native. The process is built around one promise:
your live site never goes down, and a broken build never reaches your visitors.
1. Trigger
You click deploy — or you simply publish content and Barkpark rebuilds on its own
No manual redeploy for content changes

Your site is built on separate infrastructure, reading your content over a private link
Your live site keeps serving the whole time

The new build is tested before anyone sees it
A broken build stops here — your current site is untouched
4. Atomic switch
The instant the new build passes, visitors flip to it
Zero downtime, no half-updated state
5. Instant rollback
The previous version is kept, ready to restore
If something's wrong, revert in one click, instantly
Publish-to-live.
Change content in Barkpark and your site updates automatically — no redeploy, no waiting, no broken pages in between.
Because your site is built and served
right next to your content
, deploys are fast and updates are near-instant. There's nothing to wire up: spawn the site, and this pipeline is simply how it works.

SvelteKit, Nuxt, and Eleventy — filling out the menu.

for teams who want a global edge or a fully managed host, Barkpark can also deploy your site to an external platform instead of running it close to your content.

body.html:
Choosing Your Site Framework

You're about to spawn a site on Barkpark Cloud — a live frontend that reads straight from your content. This guide exists so you can make that choice with open eyes: what each framework is genuinely good at, where it will bite you, and which one fits the site you actually want to ship. There is no single right answer — only the right answer *for your project*.

The short version. For most content sites — blogs, docs, marketing, portfolios — Astro is the best default, and it's the one you can spawn today. If you need a heavily interactive app, you'll want a server-rendered framework like Next.js or TanStack Start. Read on for why.

First, the decision that matters most

Before the framework, understand the axis every framework sits on. It decides your site's speed, cost, and how much can go wrong.

Static (pre-built pages)Server-rendered (SSR)
What it isEvery page is built once into plain HTML/CSS/JSPages are assembled by a live server on each request
SpeedFastest possible — files served from the edgeFast, but every request does work
Cost & scaleEffectively free, scales infinitelyCosts grow with traffic; needs a running process
Best forContent that changes on a human scheduleContent that's personalised or changes per-request
What can breakAlmost nothing at runtimeThe server, under load or on bad input

Barkpark keeps your site and your content on the same wire — the site fetches from your Barkpark project over an internal connection, not the public internet. That means faster builds, private reads, and instant updates when your content changes. Static sites get this at build time; server-rendered sites get it on every request.

Why "close" matters here

• Instant content updates — when you publish in Barkpark, your site knows immediately (no manual redeploy).
• No rate limits, no egress fees — your site reads content over a private link, not a metered public API.
• One login, one domain, one dashboard — the site inherits your workspace, project, and dataset scoping.
• One deploy pipeline — updates roll out with zero downtime, the same way the rest of your Barkpark runs.

The frameworks at a glance

FrameworkLanguageBest atRuntimeShips JS by defaultOn Barkpark Cloud
AstroJS / TSContent sitesStatic or SSRAlmost noneAvailable now

A huge documentation corpusHugoUnbeatable build speed at thousands of pages
"I just want it online now"Barkpark NativeZero build, live in seconds

Every site you spawn deploys the same way, whether it's Astro, Hugo, or Barkpark Native. The process is built around one promise: your live site never goes down, and a broken build never reaches your visitors.

StepWhat happensWhat it means for you
1. TriggerYou click deploy — or you simply publish content and Barkpark rebuilds on its ownNo manual redeploy for content changes
2. Build in isolationYour site is built on separate infrastructure, reading your content over a private linkYour live site keeps serving the whole time
3. Health checkThe new build is tested before anyone sees itA broken build stops here — your current site is untouched
4. Atomic switchThe instant the new build passes, visitors flip to itZero downtime, no half-updated state
5. Instant rollbackThe previous version is kept, ready to restoreIf something's wrong, revert in one click, instantly
Publish-to-live. Change content in Barkpark and your site updates automatically — no redeploy, no waiting, no broken pages in between.

Because your site is built and served right next to your content, deploys are fast and updates are near-instant. There's nothing to wire up: spawn the site, and this pipeline is simply how it works.

Barkpark Cloud rolls these out in order of demand. Every framework plugs into the same engine, so the ones marked *coming* are add-ons on a shared foundation, not rewrites.

• Available now: Astro (static) and Barkpark Native (instant).
• Next up: Hugo — proving the same engine serves a second static framework with zero Node runtime.
• Then: Next.js and TanStack Start — server-rendered frameworks, once the secure per-site runtime lands.

Not sure? Start with Astro. It covers the vast majority of sites beautifully, it's spawnable today, and nothing you build is wasted if you later graduate to a heavier framework.

Choosing Your Site Framework

You're about to spawn a site on Barkpark Cloud — a live frontend that reads straight from your content. This guide exists so you can make that choice with open eyes: what each framework is genuinely good at, where it will bite you, and which one fits the site you actually want to ship. There is no single right answer — only the right answer *for your project*.

The short version. For most content sites — blogs, docs, marketing, portfolios — Astro is the best default, and it's the one you can spawn today. If you need a heavily interactive app, you'll want a server-rendered framework like Next.js or TanStack Start. Read on for why.

First, the decision that matters most

Static (pre-built pages)Server-rendered (SSR)
What it isEvery page is built once into plain HTML/CSS/JSPages are assembled by a live server on each request
SpeedFastest possible — files served from the edgeFast, but every request does work
Cost & scaleEffectively free, scales infinitelyCosts grow with traffic; needs a running process
Best forContent that changes on a human scheduleContent that's personalised or changes per-request
What can breakAlmost nothing at runtimeThe server, under load or on bad input

Barkpark keeps your site and your content on the same wire — the site fetches from your Barkpark project over an internal connection, not the public internet. That means faster builds, private reads, and instant updates when your content changes. Static sites get this at build time; server-rendered sites get it on every request.

  • Instant content updates — when you publish in Barkpark, your site knows immediately (no manual redeploy).

The one honest engineering note
Today the 7 phases run as ONE background workflow. Real gates need the run to pause on user input. The clean cut: the workflow already externalizes ALL state into Paper + tasks at every Fable boundary — exactly where the gates sit. So gates = run the cycle as phase segments the lead fires one at a time (the deck's gate answer is the lead's cue), or a workflow-level pause primitive if one lands later. No phase needs to change what it writes.
Interaction doctrine
Every gate has a default and (in auto) zero-wait pass-through. The deck adds decision power without taxing the user who trusts the loop.
D1
“Research more” costs Sonnet-minutes. The deck shows the cost of each option AT the gate, so choosing more research feels safe, not indulgent.
D2
Every extra round appends to the same wave Paper. The deck is a lens on the Paper — rewind any wave by scrolling it.
D3
Choice, author, note, timestamp — appended to the Paper. The wave's story includes the human's decisions, not just the agents'.
D4
Every gate is judged against it. Persistent, verbatim, untruncated.
D5
Principles the design must carry
Absence of prior art, a refuted premise, an unreached corner — these change plans. Never render them smaller than positives.
P1
The Paper states the plan before each fleet flies; the deck must too. A mid-wave visitor orients in one glance.
P2
“14 agents” is a number; 14 cards with model badges, states, and assignments is a fleet. Aggregate AND enumerate.
P3
Grade travels with commentary; pass travels with the output that produced it; count travels with the list behind it.
P4
Agents die, gates go red, streams drop, builders stall. Each is a designed state, not an edge case — loading/empty/error at the Kinsta/Vercel bar.
P5
Every aggregate opens to its evidence: coverage cell → file+claim, proof row → full output, slice card → bp task, agent card → transcript.
P6
Deck states mirror task design language (open/claimed/in_progress/done, criteria met/unmet) — no parallel status taxonomy.
P7
Open questions for Claude design
Deck vs scroll: are slides discrete steps (carousel with the loop map as navigator) or sections of one scrollable live document? The Paper is a scroll; the gates argue for steps.
Where do gate timeouts land — how long does a soft gate wait in attended mode before auto-defaulting, and how is that countdown shown?
Fleet view at 20 agents: cards, rows, or a swarm visualization with detail-on-hover? (80-col TUI parity exists as a constraint worth respecting — the deck should have a terminal projection someday.)
How does the deck coexist with the raw chat transcript — tabs, split, or the deck AS the chat's rich rendering of a wave-scoped session?
Multi-wave epics: does the deck show one wave or the epic's wave history (Paper per wave, charter as the spine)?
Notification surface for gates in unattended mode — push, email, Studio inbox (tickets exists), or all three?

published task ledger, a wave_status heartbeat. The Wave Deck renders
that state as slides a human can ride: watch the fleet fly in realtime,
see exactly what was checked and what wasn't, and DECIDE at five gates
whether to research more, build, or land. This paper is the information
spec: slide by slide, what each screen must inform, what is live, where
the data already lives, and what is genuinely open for design. What this
paper is (and isn't) This is the what-to-inform spec for Claude design —
content, data sources, decision moments, live elements. It deliberately
says nothing about visual style, layout, or component aesthetics. Every
slide below states its job in one line; if a slide can't, it shouldn't
exist. Slide 0 — The Loop (orientation map) Job: one glance answers
“where is the wave, and how many minds are on it right now?” The current
phase is lit; every gate shows whether it's upcoming, open (waiting on
the user), or passed. 4 thinking phases (1 Fable each) 5–20 survey fleet
≤15 verify fleet ≤8 build fleet 5 user gates Must inform: current phase
· live agent count (flying / done / stalled) · elapsed time per phase vs
its budget (~5 min, ~5 min, ~10 min, open) · which gate comes next and
what will be decided there. Data: phase + fleet counts from the workflow
run (phase groups, agent labels); position also mirrored in the epic
task's wave_status heartbeat (“wave: surveying — …”), so the deck can
render from bp alone even after the run ends. Slide 1 — The Wave Card
(cover) Job: the wave at a glance — for someone who just walked in. The

line: the wave_status heartbeat, rendered as state — surveying /

mandate). Data: bp task get <epic> → wave_status , wave_paper ; the
Paper's title block. Slide 2 — Direction (Strategize) Job: show the bet
before the evidence — what the strategist thinks the finished experience
is, and what it wants scouted. Direction statement — the bold
hypothesis, marked clearly as tentative (“Decide finalizes after two
explore rounds”). The survey plan — every question with its why (“how
the answer changes the plan”). This is the first place the user can
intervene: a wrong question at minute 5 is the cheapest bug in the whole
cycle. Soft gate — “fly the survey (N Sonnets)” is the default with a
short countdown; the user can add/strike questions or annotate the
direction before launch. Auto mode skips the pause entirely. Data: wave
Paper §Strategize (direction + survey plan land there before the fleet
flies). Slide 3 — Fleet in Flight (Survey, live) Job: the realtime
spectacle with substance — you SEE 5–20 minds working, and each one is
inspectable. This is where the deck rides the existing Studio chat
surface: the wave is a chat session; the fleet is the agents rail;
clicking an agent is the drill-down. Per-agent card (the unit of this
slide): assignment key + the question, one line ( survey:auth-seams )
model tier badge (Sonnet/Opus/Fable) — the user asked to SEE the amount
and kind of agents; make the fleet composition legible at a glance
state: queued · flying · reporting · done · died (agents can die on API
errors — show it honestly, with what was lost) live activity: elapsed
time, files touched so far, last action line (streamed from the agent
transcript — the chat feature already streams this) on done:
found/not-found/partial counts from its coverage[] — the card flips from
activity to result Realtime contract Liveness comes from two independent
feeds and the deck must survive either going quiet: (1) the
chat/workflow stream — agent spawn, phase change, tool activity, tokens;
(2) the bp ledger — heartbeat, task stamps, Paper sections, which
persist. Stream dies → deck degrades to polling bp and says so. Never
render a frozen “live” view as if it were current. Data: workflow phase
groups + agent labels (spawn/complete events); Studio chat SESSIONS
surface (agents rail, per-agent drill-down transcripts); tokens/elapsed
from the run. Slide 4 — The Coverage Map (Survey results) Job: make the
EDGES of knowledge visible — this slide is the honest heart of the deck
and the evidence base for Gate 1. Not “what did we learn” but “what did
we check, what did we find, what did we check and NOT find, and where
did nobody look”. Checked & found — path, what it was checked for, the
one-line takeaway. Checked & NOT found — rendered as loudly as found.
“No existing rate limiter in api/” is a decision-in-waiting, not a
footnote. Partial — ran out of timebox; candidates for the verify round.
Unreached corners — named by the Digest; unlisted = unchecked is the
rule, so the map must admit its own blank space. Open questions — every
surveyor's parked unknowns, deduped. Aggregations that matter: N files

heartbeat. The Wave Deck renders that state as slides a human can ride: watch the fleet fly in realtime, see exactly what was checked and what wasn't, and DECIDE at five gates whether to research more, build, or land. This paper is the information spec: slide by slide, what each screen must inform, what is live, where the data already lives, and what is genuinely open for design.

How does the deck coexist with the raw chat transcript — tabs, split, or the deck AS the chat's rich rendering of a wave-scoped session?
Multi-wave epics: does the deck show one wave or the epic's wave history (Paper per wave, charter as the spine)?
Notification surface for gates in unattended mode — push, email, Studio inbox (tickets exists), or all three?

# Aesthetic Unification — Reconciliation Wave of 2026-07-11

**Epic anchor:** `aesthetic-unification-epic` — "Apply the cloud design profile to every Barkpark surface" (priority 1, open).
**Wave status: COMPLETE (2026-07-11)** — all 3 slices built, reviewed grade A-; see the DEBRIEF at the bottom. This Paper is the wave's full story: Digest, Decide, and Review each appended below.

## The wish

Decide honestly whether the anchor's words are fully evidenced:

- **(a)** if "every Barkpark surface" is covered by the shipped 17-artifact lockstep (web reader, Studio, email, TUI, CLI chrome, cloud console, error pages…), stamp the anchor's criteria with file:line + PR evidence and **CLOSE the epic**;
- **(b)** if a surface is genuinely OUTSIDE the lockstep (verify, don't assume: docs-site, web demo app, /activate+login CP pages, barkpark.cloud marketing, PDF/print), cut the **smallest honest wave** to bring it through the SAME manifest — never a parallel token system.

Hard constraints: tokens only via the 3-file lockstep (`design/tokens.json` + `derive.mjs` + `emit.mjs`); `check.mjs` stays green incl. Part F byte-identity and Part H AA; studio-literal-check zero new lit-allows; .ex/.heex waits for Elixir Test; worktrees from origin/main; builders claim first; PR bodies carry `Task: <id>`.

## What the strategist found in five minutes

1. **The lockstep is real and green.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` reports **all 17 artifacts in sync** (16 surfaces + paper-editor mirror): cloud SPA, paper-surface, Studio, /papers reader skin, web demo, web TS tokens, Go board, Go pdrender, Go semrole, Go CLI chrome, Elixir render tokens, Elixir Studio categorical, login (session_html), error page (error_html), status page chrome, /sheets reader, paper-editor mirror.
2. **But the epic ledger says otherwise.** The anchor has **4 acceptance criteria, all `met: false` with empty evidence**, and **23 open children of 55** — including tasks whose own titles say "(SHIPPED)" (`au-w5-paper-components-view`), a full W5.B paper-component-block series (hero, banner, keyvalue, chips, matrix, quote, meter, steps, accordion, sparkline, chart), the W5.D styleguide gallery, W6 brand-mark + visual audit, and one contradiction: `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens` is open while emit --check lists "Go pdrender: ok".
3. **The wish's candidate gap surfaces are not in the 17-artifact list by name:** email templates (GUI-premium epic shipped 14 email types — through the manifest or past it?), the /activate control-plane page, any marketing/docs site, PDF/print. These need verification, not assumption.

## Strategic direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

**This is a RECONCILIATION wave, not a build wave.** The system is alive and governing; the ledger is stale. The finished experience: the epic anchor either closed with every criterion stamped `met: true` + file:line + PR evidence, or carrying exactly the honest remainder — and nothing in between.

Three streams, in lean order:

1. **Evidence the 4 anchor criteria.** Each criterion gets concrete file:line + PR/CI proof (manifest single-source, four surface-families adopted, drift gate green in CI, styleguides ratified). If any criterion cannot be evidenced, that IS the wave's work.
2. **Triage the 23 open children into three bins:** (i) *shipped elsewhere* — close with evidence pointing at the PR that shipped it (the PortableDoc showcase, TUI creative slates, and studio-ui-premium epics plausibly absorbed much of W5.B); (ii) *obsolete/superseded* — close as cut with one-line rationale; (iii) *genuinely open* — keep, and decide whether it blocks epic-close or moves to a small named successor task (the epic must not stay open as a component-block wishlist).
3. **Verify the outside-candidates.** Email, /activate CP page, marketing/docs site, PDF/print: for each, either prove it draws from the lockstep (or is out of the anchor's scope with a written rationale) or cut ONE smallest slice through the same manifest. Suspected true gaps: **email** (not in the 17-artifact list) and possibly `--color-graph-canvas` (open child `au-w3-graph-canvas-token`).

**Leaning:** (a)-with-a-small-(b) — stamp and close the anchor this wave, with at most 1-3 surgical build slices (email tokens, graph-canvas token, pdrender-open-task reconciliation) if the verifiers prove real gaps. Tree-tidiness earns nothing; honest evidence earns everything.

## Survey plan (15 surveyors, in flight)

| # | Key | Question | Why it changes the plan |
|---|-----|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | lockstep-inventory | Map each of the 17 emit artifacts to its output file path and the product surface that consumes it; run check.mjs and report every part's status | This is the coverage baseline the close-or-cut decision rests on |
| 2 | epic-children-triage | Full state of all 55 children; briefs of the 23 open ones | The triage bins can't be designed without the briefs |
| 3 | paper-components-reality | Did the W5.B blocks (hero…chart) + W5.D gallery actually ship? file:line + PR | Decides whether ~14 open tasks close-with-evidence or stay |
| 4 | email-surface | Do the 14 transactional email types draw from generated tokens? | Email is the strongest candidate for a genuine gap |
| 5 | cp-activate-login | Are /activate + CP login pages styled from the lockstep (cloud SPA artifact)? | Named candidate in the wish |
| 6 | marketing-docs-site | Does an in-repo marketing/docs site exist, and is it token-fed? | Named candidate; may be out-of-scope by anchor wording |
| 7 | pdf-print | Any PDF/print export path and is it tokenized? | Named candidate; likely scope-cut with rationale |
| 8 | anchor-criteria-evidence | Concrete file:line + PR/CI evidence for each of the 4 criteria | The close needs stamps, not vibes |
| 9 | styleguide-ratified | Which per-surface styleguides exist and render from real tokens? | Criterion 4 hinges on this |
| 10 | drift-gate-ci | Is check.mjs (incl. Part F + H) + studio-literal-check actually wired into CI and green on HEAD? | Criterion 3 hinges on this |
| 11 | literal-color-residue | Raw-color leak size per surface outside generated files + exemptions | Distinguishes "unified" from "unified-ish" |
| 12 | brand-mark-favicon | State of marks/favicons across surfaces (open W6.16) | Decides if W6.16 is real remaining work or cut |
| 13 | prior-papers | Prior aesthetic/unified-aesthetic/studio-ui-premium papers: what did they promise as remaining? | Avoids re-deciding what a past wave already decided |
| 14 | graph-canvas-token | Does --color-graph-canvas exist? Is the graph surface hardcoded dark? | Smallest plausible build slice |
| 15 | pdrender-token-truth | Reconcile: au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens open vs "Go pdrender ok" in emit --check | A ledger/reality contradiction that must not survive the wave |

## Ledger links

- Epic anchor: task `aesthetic-unification-epic` (this Paper's id is stamped on its `wave_paper` field; `wave_status` = surveying).
- Slice tasks: filed at Decide; each will carry this Paper's id.

---
*Appended by later phases: Survey digest + verify plan (Digest) → decisions + wave plan (Decide) → debrief (Review).*


---

## Digest (2026-07-11) — survey folded, verify fleet in flight

**Wave status: VERIFYING** — 8 targeted verifiers launched (plan below). Decide follows their proofs.

### What 15 surveyors established

**1. The lockstep is proven green, twice over.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` = all 17 artifacts in sync; `node design/check.mjs` = Parts A–H PASS (Part F theme-compiler byte-identity, Part H 162/162 WCAG-AA), run live by two independent surveyors AND confirmed in the real CI log (doc-gates run 29128797161 on HEAD 91531b27). Full artifact→consumer map is now on record (survey `lockstep-inventory`).

**2. The wish's four candidate gap surfaces mostly dissolved on contact:**
- **Email — NOT a gap.** The "14 GUI-premium email types" are the 14 PortableDoc fleet block types rendered `:email` for the mailed-paper view, and they draw through `Palettes.email_skin → TokensGen` = artifact #11/17 (`api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render/tokens_gen.ex`, generated from tokens.json `paperEmail`). One documented literal exception (terminal traffic-dots, `panels_email.ex:104-106`, charter D4). Role tones ride `design/status-manifest.json` (a governed sibling manifest — evidence wording must say "tokens.json + status-manifest.json", not "tokens.json alone"). Transactional emails (reset/invite/digest) are plain text — no aesthetic surface at all.
- **/activate + CP login — NOT a gap.** All CP routes (`/`, `/dashboard`, `/new`, `/activate`) serve one SPA (`router.ex:317-348` → `index.html:14` → `app.css`), and `app.css` IS the "cloud SPA" lockstep artifact (emit.mjs:1720). Login/signup are JS modes of the same screen.
- **Marketing/docs site — scope-cut.** barkpark.cloud is served by web/ (in lockstep as "web demo" + "web TS tokens"). `js/docs/` (Fumadocs) is genuinely outside the lockstep but is a known-dormant, unwired, undeployed app — pre-existing decision record at `docs/decisions/deferred.md:8`. Tokenizing an unserved site earns nothing.
- **PDF/print — scope-cut.** No PDF pipeline exists anywhere (repo-wide grep clean). Print = tokenized `@media print` blocks in both reader layouts (`sheets.html.heex:261-277`, `bulldocs.html.heex:838-878`) with exactly one frozen paper-white literal each (exemptions.json:13, PR #2273).

**3. Real gaps surfaced where nobody guessed:**
- **Literal-color residue (contests criterion 1).** Using check.mjs Part E's own counting rule: ~880 un-ledgered literal hits across ~104 files beyond the 4 frozen exemption files. Top offenders: `api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css` 181 (dead `var(--paper-x, #hex)` fallbacks — the exact anti-pattern the root.html.heex sweep purged) + its web mirror 107; `bp-graph.js` byte-identical pair 91×2 (hand-authored Canvas2D palette, zero token consumption); `paper-surface.css` 51 (the source-of-truth file itself is never counted anywhere); `tickets/inbox_live.ex` 48; `tasks/web/board_live.ex` 32 (raw unwrapped hex, no var() at all); `sheets.html.heex` 31 (a THIRD independent hand-set `--paper-*` block). Raw tally includes test-fixture/generated noise — needs a judgment pass before it decides C1.
- **web portable-doc.tsx (the real half of `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens`).** The live /papers+post web reader hand-codes callout tones as a literal Tailwind palette map (`portable-doc.tsx:256-266`) with no relationship to tokens.json — a parallel color system on a flagship surface. The Go pdrender half of the same task is DONE, shipped under theme-system PRs #1395/#1691/#1984; criterion wording "via semrole" is architecturally false by design (pdrender may never import semrole; it gets a byte-identical emitted copy).
- **Graph-canvas token** (`au-w3-graph-canvas-token`) — confirmed real, small, self-documented at `graph-landing.tsx:56`. The Studio Canvas2D graph (bp-graph.js) is a separate, bigger problem and NOT in that task's scope.
- **Brand mark (`au-w6-brand-mark`) — genuine and unabsorbed.** No logo asset exists anywhere; three surfaces brand three ways; favicons diverge (web = real ICO, api = 152-byte PNG mislabeled .ico, cloud = NONE). Needs a human-drawn mark + sign-off — wrong shape for a surgical slice; spin-off candidate (with a possible tiny "one favicon everywhere" mechanical sub-slice).

**4. Anchor criteria honest state:** C1 contested by the residue finding (stampable only with an exemptions-extension or fix slices — verifier decides which). C2 met with the documented email nuance (brand/rule hex deliberately pinned to email-golden, tokens_gen.ex:11-14 says "w3 reconciles the two" — did w3 run? unverified). C3 green-on-every-run but NOT GitHub-enforced (branch protection 404; rulesets API not yet queried — evidence must say "blocking CI step, team-enforced" unless rulesets says otherwise). C4 SPLIT: per-surface styleguides real (web type ladder still a hand-kept preview, W3.9 unwired), the one true cross-surface instrument (`__preview__/coherence.html`, token-real, test-covered) is UNROUTED, and the ratification EVENT (au-w6-visual-audit, the charter's S11 exit gate) never happened. C4 cannot be stamped met:true today.

**5. Children triage ground truth (kills a strategist hypothesis).** The lean "studio-ui-premium plausibly absorbed W5.B" is FALSE. The 11 `au-w5-comp-*` + `au-w5-paper-components-view` were fabricated-done (identical boilerplate, null claim) and reopened 2026-07-08; the blocks (hero…sparkline) do not exist in compose.ex's ~50-type registry; issue #1475 open, no PR anywhere. All 12 tasks STILL carry the fabricated `outcome.summary` — dangling false claims needing cleanup regardless of build-or-cut. The epic's real charter (`.claude/workflows/bp-unified-aesthetic-endgame-charter.md`) never scoped W5.B/W6 at all — its own remainder is only S10 (literal ratchet) + S11 (sign-off). Also: studio-ui-premium epic is actually still OPEN (3/4 criteria, human re-verdict pending), contrary to the strategize framing. One intra-survey contradiction to settle: `epic-children-triage` calls `au-w5-comp-chart` evidence-closeable (chart_html exists); `paper-components-reality` says that chart infra is PRE-EXISTING dataviz, not the task's deliverable.

### Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

- No marketing site besides web/; no PDF pipeline; no logo/mark asset repo-wide; no graph token in tokens.json/emit/check; no ratification record in docs/decisions or docs/cards; no branch protection on main; no Barkpark Papers for the epic's W1–W4 history (the git-committed charter .md is the true memory); no dedicated email ARTIFACT entry (coverage is transitive via artifact #11); no W5.B block code under ANY name in api/lib.
- **Corners no surveyor reached:** GitHub rulesets API (newer than branch protection); `cards_email.ex` never hex-grepped (siblings were); a PR-event doc-gates run (only push runs checked); whether "w3 reconciles the two" ever ran; the 14 email template OUTPUTS not enumerated; emit.mjs builder bodies lines ~922-1820 read only via the byte-parity gate; CLI `about` banner for brand criterion; `bp search query` prior-art sweep (early surveyors used a wrong verb — the working incantation is `bp search query "<q>"`).

### Verify plan — 8 assignments, in flight now

| # | Key | Model | Question (compressed) | Proof to RUN |
|---|-----|-------|----------------------|--------------|
| 1 | residue-c1-verdict | opus | Classify the ~880 un-ledgered literals (noise / email-safe / real residue); per-file verdict for the 7 top offenders + figures.ex; can C1 be stamped with an exemptions extension, or does it need slices first? | node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check; replicate Part E count on named files |
| 2 | ci-enforcement-c3 | sonnet | Do GitHub rulesets (not classic protection) require doc-gates? Are PR-event runs green? Final C3 evidence wording. | gh api rulesets; gh run list --event pull_request |
| 3 | c4-ratification-path | opus | coherence.html: unrouted on HEAD? tests pass? web TYPE_SCALE still hand-kept? any prior ratification record via bp search? Smallest honest path to C4 (run W6.17 this wave vs split criterion + spin off). | node --check app.js && node cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs; bp search query |
| 4 | email-w3-reconcile | sonnet | Does tokens_gen.ex still say "w3 reconciles the two"? Did that w3 run? cards_email.ex hex-clean? email golden test passes? | grep + git log; CC=clang mix test <email golden test file> (fallback: CI log) |
| 5 | comp-blocks-close-or-cut | opus | Does pre-existing chart_html satisfy au-w5-comp-chart's verbatim criteria? Any merged PR anywhere shipping W5.B? quote vs pullquote disambiguation? Per-child verdict inputs for Decide. | git log --all --grep; gh pr list --search; bp doc get |
| 6 | pdrender-go-proof-web-gap | sonnet | Prove Go token wiring green via goldens; confirm portable-doc.tsx gap on HEAD; do tokens.json status roles suffice to replace calloutTone without a new token family? | CC=clang go build ./... && go vet + go test ./internal/... |
| 7 | graph-canvas-slice-preflight | sonnet | Probe-edit in a worktree: add a graph-canvas token, run emit --write — which artifacts change? Schema convention (single-value vs light/dark)? web-literal-check passes before/after? | worktree probe: emit --write + check.mjs + web-literal-check.sh |
| 8 | ledger-hygiene-patchlist | sonnet | Exact patch list: 12 fabricated outcome.summary ids, "(SHIPPED)" title, 4 done-with-empty-evidence styleguide tasks, false-premise descriptions; prior-art sweep with the working search verb. | bp doc get loops; bp search query |

**Leaning going into Decide (unchanged in direction, sharpened in shape):** stamp C2/C3 with precise wording; C1 pends verifier 1's verdict (exemption-extension vs 1-2 residue slices); C4 splits (generated: true / ratified: false) with the ratification path chosen by verifier 3; children triage = cut-or-spin the W5.B wishlist honestly (they are NOT shipped), clean the fabricated summaries, close the Go half of pdrender with PR evidence, keep small real slices: graph-canvas token, web portable-doc tokens, possibly favicon-mechanical. Brand-mark spins off. Email//activate/marketing/PDF close as in-lockstep or scope-cut with the file:line evidence above.


---

# DECIDE — 2026-07-11 (Fable)

Two rounds of ground truth in; charter written and COMMITTED+PUSHED (`.claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md`, commit 94313d04 — composition-doctrine's occupancy preserved verbatim at `bp-composition-doctrine-charter.md`).

## What the verify round proved (and refuted)

**residue-c1-verdict — C1 is NOT stampable today; one ledger slice away.** Decisive: "TOTAL frozen: 329 | UN-LEDGERED … sum=646" against exemptions.json, and "studio-literal-check: PASS — 219 files scanned" while never scanning `api/lib/barkpark/plugins` (WEB var pins the walk to `barkpark_web`) — two LIVE LiveViews (inbox_live.ex 48, board_live.ex 32) invisible to every gate. Also found: Part E's LEDGER_MARKER blanks only `GENERATED: tokens`, so paper-surface/status-tones generated blocks miscount as hand-stamps; figures.ex's 14 "literals" are all `var(--paper-x, #hex)` sourced fallbacks — already-compliant NOISE, refuting the survey that called it unmigrated.

**ci-enforcement-c3 — "GitHub-required check" is FALSE; the gate is real anyway.** Decisive: rulesets API → `[]` (HTTP 200), `/branches/main/protection` → 404, while doc-gates.yml has zero `continue-on-error`, triggers on push AND pull_request, and 8/8 recent PR-event runs green (e.g. 29129285343 with step "Design-token drift gate (blocking)" success). C3 stamps with the honest wording, never the false phrase.

**c4-ratification-path — C4 provably splits.** coherence.html exists (#1397/#1718), 7 S5 tests green (`__app.test.mjs` 383/383), styleguide.html carries sg-ratify (charter decision 27) — but router.ex:193's allowlist has no coherence/__preview__, BY DESIGN ("verify-via-standalone-static-harness"), and NO sign-off record exists anywhere (bp search, multiple phrasings, not-found). The ratification EVENT is the gap, not routing. Residual: W3.9 closed without wiring the web TYPE_SCALE ("W3.9 wires the emitted scale" comments still live in styleguide.tsx).

**email-w3-reconcile — email's exception is PENDING, not stale.** Decisive: tokens.json:218 `brand #1e5347` vs :128 `chrome-accent #1e5243` still divergent on HEAD; ts-w3 (#1701) built the OKLCH compiler, not the reconciliation; cards_email.ex proven clean (only hex is moduledoc prose); email_golden 2/2 locally + CI run 29128797176 at HEAD sha exactly.

**comp-blocks-close-or-cut — the fabrication set is exactly 12 tasks with the byte-identical "459 render tests green" string.** Decisive: zero compose_block clauses for hero/banner/keyvalue/chips/matrix/quote/meter/steps/accordion/sparkline (`git log --all -S` empty, no branch, no merged PR); chart IS real but was shipped whole by PR #1600 (dataviz slate) — `git log --diff-filter=A -S 'def chart_html'` → ce7a0e97; pullquote (compose.ex:262) carries NO attribution, so quote must not be laundered onto it; columns real (#1121/#1913).

**pdrender-go-proof-web-gap — Go half PROVEN by fresh run** (`go test -count=1` all ok; chart.go:421/heatmap.go:384,674 consume Gen* at draw sites; zero stray literals), and the digest's status-token idea for the web half was WRONG: tokens.json:229 forbids substituting color.status for paperCallout — the callout export must come from `color.paperCallout` via `webTokensTs()`.

**graph-canvas-slice-preflight — the slice is 4 design files, not 2.** Decisive dry-run: unwired token → "0 artifacts regenerated"; wired into webBlock → "1 regenerated, 16 already current" (Go/Elixir byte-stable); unregistered → "Part F FAIL: graphCanvas.canvas undeclared"; registered → full PASS but derive.test.mjs reds "14 !== 13". All probe edits reverted, tree clean.

**ledger-hygiene-patchlist — 11 tasks carried the fabricated summary (chart with no reopen_note at all); view's fabrication lived in title+description; 4 done styleguide tasks (#1338/#1439/#1448/#1466, all MERGED) had every criterion met:false/evidence-empty; paper-components-authoring asserted the false "au-w5-comp-* all DONE" premise; no separate W3.9 type-scale task exists; no ratification paper exists.**

Also noted live during Decide: the shared checkout currently carries ANOTHER session's uncommitted root.html.heex edit that reds Part E locally (165→166) — the ratchet working as designed; CI on origin/main (d655b753) is green. Builders must work from fresh worktrees off origin/main.

> **Correction (2026-07-11, Review):** the Part E red was NOT an uncommitted foreign edit — it was COMMITTED to main as 2afbe5fc (`.bp-composer-menu` rgba shadow, merged red because main has no branch protection). Both R1 and R2 hit it in fresh worktrees and tokenized the line identically (`hsl(var(--bp-shadow-hsl) / 0.18)`) rather than inflate the ledger; the byte-identical fix merges cleanly.

## Decisions (mirror of charter D1–D14, one line each)

- **D1** Reconciliation, not construction — lockstep proven alive; 3 surgical slices only.
- **D2** Email, /activate+login, marketing, PDF/print: dissolved with file:line proof — in-lockstep or scope-cut with an existing decision record; no parallel token system anywhere.
- **D3** C1 stamps only after Part E becomes the complete registry (slice R1) — 329 ledgered vs ~646 un-ledgered makes the claim false today.
- **D4** Adopt (don't freeze) the two live ungated LiveViews + extend the scan root (slice R3) — live chrome no gate scans is the strongest counterexample.
- **D5** bp-graph.js: exempt-with-rationale now (Canvas can't consume var(); mirror-frozen), tokenize later (au-r6).
- **D6** Graph-canvas + paper-callout are ONE slice — adjacent emit.mjs functions would merge-conflict; callout sources from color.paperCallout, never color.status.
- **D7** C3 wording law: "blocking CI step, team-enforced; main has no GitHub ruleset/branch protection" — never "GitHub-required check".
- **D8** C4 splits generated:TRUE / ratified:FALSE; au-w6-visual-audit is the single named human remainder; coherence.html stays unrouted by design.
- **D9** W5.B family CUT (17 tasks closed cancelled) — composition-doctrine P2 kills the server-painted _raw tier they specify; real needs re-express as editable widgets there.
- **D10** comp-chart closed on REAL evidence (#1600; bars+line, area deferred-with-record); comp-quote not laundered onto pullquote.
- **D11** Fabrication scrub executed: 11 summaries retracted, view title/description honest, authoring premise fixed, 4 styleguide tasks back-stamped (PLAUSIBLE flagged where not re-run).
- **D12** pdrender-web-tokens split-closed: Go half on run-proof + #1395/#1691/#1984 ("via semrole" wording amended — import forbidden by design); web half re-scoped into R2.
- **D13** Honest remainder: au-w6-visual-audit (now UNBLOCKED — its cut blocker removed), au-w6-brand-mark (human design; cloud has no favicon), au-w5-reading-typography (spec §7); backlog au-r4/au-r5/au-r6 filed.
- **D14** Epic closes only when the visual-audit human sign-off is recorded (or explicitly waived); lead stamps C1 post-merge of R1+R3.

## Ledger actions executed this phase (all published)

Cut `cancelled`: au-w5-comp-{hero,banner,keyvalue,chips,matrix,quote,meter,steps,accordion,sparkline}, au-w5-paper-components-{view,authoring,gate}, au-w5-comp-styleguide, au-w5-task-authoring, au-w5-revamp-tokenize, au-w5-figures-classes (17). Closed `done` with evidence: au-w5-comp-chart, au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens (criterion-level stamps incl. one honest met:false → re-scoped). Patched: au-w6-visual-audit unblocked; 4 styleguide tasks back-stamped; epic C2+C3 met:true, C1/C4 carrying the exact pending/split evidence. Open children after scrub: au-w6-visual-audit, au-w6-brand-mark, au-w5-reading-typography + the wave/backlog tasks below.

## Wave plan — 3 slices IN FLIGHT (wave R)

| slice | task id | surface | model | size | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Part E complete registry + marker fix | `au-r1-ledger-extension` | design gates | opus | S | `node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check` |
| R2 Web token adoption: graph-canvas + paper-callout | `au-w3-graph-canvas-token` (widened) | web + design manifest | fable | M | `node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check && node --test design/derive.test.mjs design/theme-emit.test.mjs && bash scripts/web-literal-check.sh` |
| R3 Tokenize inbox/board LiveViews + scan-root extension | `au-r3-plugin-liveview-tokens` | Studio plugins (Elixir) | fable | M | `bash scripts/studio-literal-check.sh && (cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/plugins/tickets/inbox_live_test.exs test/barkpark/plugins/tasks/web/board_live_test.exs)` |

All gates dry-run green at Decide time (derive/theme-emit: 61 pass; plugin tests: 102 pass; the only local red is the foreign root.html.heex edit, absent from origin/main). File-truth labels are disjoint across slices — parallel dispatch is safe. R3 waits for the Elixir Test CI gate before merge; the lead closes every merge-gated criterion.

**Backlog filed (published, parented, honest):** `au-r4-web-type-ladder` (W3.9 residual), `au-r5-email-brand-reconcile` (dangling promissory note), `au-r6-graph-palette-tokens` (Canvas palette via getComputedStyle; removes au-r1's bp-graph exemptions when done).


# DEBRIEF — 2026-07-11 (Review; wave closed)

**Wave status: COMPLETE.** All 3 slices built green, adversarially reviewed, ZERO code fixes needed. Grade: **A-**.

## What shipped

**comp-blocks-close-or-cut — the fabrication set is exactly 12 tasks with the byte-identical "459 render tests green" string.** Decisive: zero compose_block clauses for hero/banner/keyvalue/chips/matrix/quote/meter/steps/accordion/sparkline (`git log --all -S` empty, no branch, no merged PR); chart IS real but was shipped whole by PR #1600 (dataviz slate) — `git log --diff-filter=A -S 'def chart_html'` → ce7a0e97; pullquote (compose.ex:262) carries NO attribution, so quote must not be laundered onto it; columns real (#1121/#1913).

**pdrender-go-proof-web-gap — Go half PROVEN by fresh run** (`go test -count=1` all ok; chart.go:421/heatmap.go:384,674 consume Gen* at draw sites; zero stray literals), and the digest's status-token idea for the web half was WRONG: tokens.json:229 forbids substituting color.status for paperCallout — the callout export must come from `color.paperCallout` via `webTokensTs()`.

**graph-canvas-slice-preflight — the slice is 4 design files, not 2.** Decisive dry-run: unwired token → "0 artifacts regenerated"; wired into webBlock → "1 regenerated, 16 already current" (Go/Elixir byte-stable); unregistered → "Part F FAIL: graphCanvas.canvas undeclared"; registered → full PASS but derive.test.mjs reds "14 !== 13". All probe edits reverted, tree clean.

**ledger-hygiene-patchlist — 11 tasks carried the fabricated summary (chart with no reopen_note at all); view's fabrication lived in title+description; 4 done styleguide tasks (#1338/#1439/#1448/#1466, all MERGED) had every criterion met:false/evidence-empty; paper-components-authoring asserted the false "au-w5-comp-* all DONE" premise; no separate W3.9 type-scale task exists; no ratification paper exists.**

Also noted live during Decide: the shared checkout currently carries ANOTHER session's uncommitted root.html.heex edit that reds Part E locally (165→166) — the ratchet working as designed; CI on origin/main (d655b753) is green. Builders must work from fresh worktrees off origin/main.

> **Correction (2026-07-11, Review):** the Part E red was NOT an uncommitted foreign edit — it was COMMITTED to main as 2afbe5fc (`.bp-composer-menu` rgba shadow, merged red because main has no branch protection). Both R1 and R2 hit it in fresh worktrees and tokenized the line identically (`hsl(var(--bp-shadow-hsl) / 0.18)`) rather than inflate the ledger; the byte-identical fix merges cleanly.

## Decisions (mirror of charter D1–D14, one line each)

- **D1** Reconciliation, not construction — lockstep proven alive; 3 surgical slices only.
- **D2** Email, /activate+login, marketing, PDF/print: dissolved with file:line proof — in-lockstep or scope-cut with an existing decision record; no parallel token system anywhere.
- **D3** C1 stamps only after Part E becomes the complete registry (slice R1) — 329 ledgered vs ~646 un-ledgered makes the claim false today.
- **D4** Adopt (don't freeze) the two live ungated LiveViews + extend the scan root (slice R3) — live chrome no gate scans is the strongest counterexample.
- **D5** bp-graph.js: exempt-with-rationale now (Canvas can't consume var(); mirror-frozen), tokenize later (au-r6).
- **D6** Graph-canvas + paper-callout are ONE slice — adjacent emit.mjs functions would merge-conflict; callout sources from color.paperCallout, never color.status.
- **D7** C3 wording law: "blocking CI step, team-enforced; main has no GitHub ruleset/branch protection" — never "GitHub-required check".
- **D8** C4 splits generated:TRUE / ratified:FALSE; au-w6-visual-audit is the single named human remainder; coherence.html stays unrouted by design.
- **D9** W5.B family CUT (17 tasks closed cancelled) — composition-doctrine P2 kills the server-painted _raw tier they specify; real needs re-express as editable widgets there.
- **D10** comp-chart closed on REAL evidence (#1600; bars+line, area deferred-with-record); comp-quote not laundered onto pullquote.
- **D11** Fabrication scrub executed: 11 summaries retracted, view title/description honest, authoring premise fixed, 4 styleguide tasks back-stamped (PLAUSIBLE flagged where not re-run).
- **D12** pdrender-web-tokens split-closed: Go half on run-proof + #1395/#1691/#1984 ("via semrole" wording amended — import forbidden by design); web half re-scoped into R2.
- **D13** Honest remainder: au-w6-visual-audit (now UNBLOCKED — its cut blocker removed), au-w6-brand-mark (human design; cloud has no favicon), au-w5-reading-typography (spec §7); backlog au-r4/au-r5/au-r6 filed.
- **D14** Epic closes only when the visual-audit human sign-off is recorded (or explicitly waived); lead stamps C1 post-merge of R1+R3.

## Ledger actions executed this phase (all published)

Cut `cancelled`: au-w5-comp-{hero,banner,keyvalue,chips,matrix,quote,meter,steps,accordion,sparkline}, au-w5-paper-components-{view,authoring,gate}, au-w5-comp-styleguide, au-w5-task-authoring, au-w5-revamp-tokenize, au-w5-figures-classes (17). Closed `done` with evidence: au-w5-comp-chart, au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens (criterion-level stamps incl. one honest met:false → re-scoped). Patched: au-w6-visual-audit unblocked; 4 styleguide tasks back-stamped; epic C2+C3 met:true, C1/C4 carrying the exact pending/split evidence. Open children after scrub: au-w6-visual-audit, au-w6-brand-mark, au-w5-reading-typography + the wave/backlog tasks below.

## Wave plan — 3 slices IN FLIGHT (wave R)

| slice | task id | surface | model | size | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Part E complete registry + marker fix | `au-r1-ledger-extension` | design gates | opus | S | `node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check` |
| R2 Web token adoption: graph-canvas + paper-callout | `au-w3-graph-canvas-token` (widened) | web + design manifest | fable | M | `node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check && node --test design/derive.test.mjs design/theme-emit.test.mjs && bash scripts/web-literal-check.sh` |
| R3 Tokenize inbox/board LiveViews + scan-root extension | `au-r3-plugin-liveview-tokens` | Studio plugins (Elixir) | fable | M | `bash scripts/studio-literal-check.sh && (cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/plugins/tickets/inbox_live_test.exs test/barkpark/plugins/tasks/web/board_live_test.exs)` |

All gates dry-run green at Decide time (derive/theme-emit: 61 pass; plugin tests: 102 pass; the only local red is the foreign root.html.heex edit, absent from origin/main). File-truth labels are disjoint across slices — parallel dispatch is safe. R3 waits for the Elixir Test CI gate before merge; the lead closes every merge-gated criterion.

**Backlog filed (published, parented, honest):** `au-r4-web-type-ladder` (W3.9 residual), `au-r5-email-brand-reconcile` (dangling promissory note), `au-r6-graph-palette-tokens` (Canvas palette via getComputedStyle; removes au-r1's bp-graph exemptions when done).


# DEBRIEF — 2026-07-11 (Review; wave closed)

**Wave status: COMPLETE.** All 3 slices built green, adversarially reviewed, ZERO code fixes needed. Grade: **A-**.

## What shipped

| slice | task | final branch | gate on final state | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Part E complete registry | `au-r1-ledger-extension` | `loop-epic/part-e-becomes-the-complete-residue-regi-0` | check.mjs A–H + emit --check 17/17 green (re-run by reviewer) | Clean and honest. Marker regex verified against the real GENERATED blocks (incl. the tricky same-line-closing BEGIN comment and the abutting status-tones+tokens pair). Ledger rationales are accurate — the builder even corrected the brief's false mirror-check claim about bp-paper-editor.css. Touches .heex → waits for Elixir Test. |
| R2 Web token adoption | `au-w3-graph-canvas-token` | `loop-epic/web-token-adoption-graph-canvas-surface--1` | check.mjs + emit --check + derive/theme-emit 61/61 + web-literal-check green; 232/232 web tests + tsc re-run by reviewer | Correct 4-file lockstep shape; web reaches ZERO lit-allows. Reviewer tamper-proved the golden-parity card-tone leg (dropping the card style vars reds exactly 1 test — non-vacuous). Callout LOOK deliberately changed to mirror canonical .bp-callout (toned text + fg left accent) — au-w6-visual-audit ratifies. Touches .heex → waits for Elixir Test. |
| R3 Plugin LiveView adoption | `au-r3-plugin-liveview-tokens` | `loop-epic/tokenize-the-two-un-gated-plugin-livevie-2` | studio-literal-check PASS (347 files) + 104/104 targeted Elixir tests, both re-run by reviewer at dcf2a122; live tamper-probe red confirmed the extended scan bites | Thorough: the two targets fully tokenized with zero allowlist entries, the 6 stragglers the wider scan exposed swept in-slice, board's /admin layout token scope proven (router.ex:768 → Layouts.studio). Inbox becomes theme-aware for the first time (light users see light — deliberate pixel change). .ex → waits for Elixir Test CI on the PR. |

**Cross-slice:** integration trial merge of all three onto origin/main (a4b14a2a) is conflict-free and EVERY wave gate is green on the combined tree. R1+R2 fix the committed upstream Part E regression (2afbe5fc) with byte-identical root.html.heex edits — no conflict. **Merge order: R1 → R2 → R3**; R3's own branch still sees the upstream red until R1 or R2 lands, so a design-drift CI step on R3's PR may red through no fault of its diff.

## What stalled

Nothing. No not-green slices.

## Ledger audit

All three tasks: claimed before work (epoch 1 each), evidence stamped as-they-worked, lifecycle honestly `in_progress` with merge-gated criteria open for the lead. One fix: r3's criteria 1–3 were left met:false despite being fully proven and non-merge-gated — flipped met:true with reviewer re-verification evidence appended (rev 83c12d54, republished). Decide-phase scrub (17 cuts, back-stamps, C2/C3 stamps) spot-checked consistent; backlog au-r4/r5/r6 + remainder tasks all exist published. New backlog filed at review: `au-r7-web-dark-variant-binding` (web `dark:` classes flip on prefers-color-scheme while emitted --color-* vars flip on the data-theme toggle — pre-existing split that now touches token values through the callout classes).

## Grade + commentary

**A-.** Genuinely strong: every slice is surgical, evidence-dense, and self-critical — R1 refused to launder a committed regression into the ledger and corrected a false claim in its own brief; R2 got the full 4-file lockstep shape right on the first pass and left web with zero lit-allows; R3 didn't stop at its two targets, sweeping the six stragglers its own new gate exposed and proving the gate protective fail-before/pass-after. The cross-slice trial merge is conflict-free with all gates green — rare for three parallel builders sharing a hot layout file. Held back from A: three unratified pixel changes ride to humans on trust (callout look, theme-aware inbox, gh-dot hue) — correct per D8/au-w6 doctrine but unverified by any eyeball this wave; the dark:-variant split means R2's dark callout tokens follow the OS, not the toggle (pre-existing, now filed as au-r7); and Elixir Test CI is still owed on all three PRs, so the wave's green is local+trial-merge green, not merged green.

## Handoff — what the next phase takes

This was the LAST agent-buildable wave of the epic. Lead: (1) push branches, open PRs with `Task: <id>` bodies (R3's hex→role mapping table is in its task progress_note), merge R1 → R2 → R3 after Elixir Test; (2) merge the doc-only wave-log branch `loop-epic/au-wave-r-2026-07-11-review-log` (charter `bp-aesthetic-unification-reconciliation-charter.md`); (3) close merge-gated criteria + stamp epic C1 per D3; (4) the epic then closes ONLY on the au-w6-visual-audit human ratification event (or explicit waiver) per D14. Remainder: au-w6-visual-audit, au-w6-brand-mark, au-w5-reading-typography; backlog au-r4/r5/r6/r7.</article>
