# Aesthetic Unification — Reconciliation Wave of 2026-07-11

**Epic anchor:** `aesthetic-unification-epic` — "Apply the cloud design profile to every Barkpark surface" (priority 1, open).
**Wave status: COMPLETE (2026-07-11)** — all 3 slices built, reviewed grade A-; see the DEBRIEF at the bottom. This Paper is the wave's full story: Digest, Decide, and Review each appended below.

## The wish

Decide honestly whether the anchor's words are fully evidenced:

- **(a)** if "every Barkpark surface" is covered by the shipped 17-artifact lockstep (web reader, Studio, email, TUI, CLI chrome, cloud console, error pages…), stamp the anchor's criteria with file:line + PR evidence and **CLOSE the epic**;
- **(b)** if a surface is genuinely OUTSIDE the lockstep (verify, don't assume: docs-site, web demo app, /activate+login CP pages, barkpark.cloud marketing, PDF/print), cut the **smallest honest wave** to bring it through the SAME manifest — never a parallel token system.

Hard constraints: tokens only via the 3-file lockstep (`design/tokens.json` + `derive.mjs` + `emit.mjs`); `check.mjs` stays green incl. Part F byte-identity and Part H AA; studio-literal-check zero new lit-allows; .ex/.heex waits for Elixir Test; worktrees from origin/main; builders claim first; PR bodies carry `Task: <id>`.

## What the strategist found in five minutes

1. **The lockstep is real and green.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` reports **all 17 artifacts in sync** (16 surfaces + paper-editor mirror): cloud SPA, paper-surface, Studio, /papers reader skin, web demo, web TS tokens, Go board, Go pdrender, Go semrole, Go CLI chrome, Elixir render tokens, Elixir Studio categorical, login (session_html), error page (error_html), status page chrome, /sheets reader, paper-editor mirror.
2. **But the epic ledger says otherwise.** The anchor has **4 acceptance criteria, all `met: false` with empty evidence**, and **23 open children of 55** — including tasks whose own titles say "(SHIPPED)" (`au-w5-paper-components-view`), a full W5.B paper-component-block series (hero, banner, keyvalue, chips, matrix, quote, meter, steps, accordion, sparkline, chart), the W5.D styleguide gallery, W6 brand-mark + visual audit, and one contradiction: `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens` is open while emit --check lists "Go pdrender: ok".
3. **The wish's candidate gap surfaces are not in the 17-artifact list by name:** email templates (GUI-premium epic shipped 14 email types — through the manifest or past it?), the /activate control-plane page, any marketing/docs site, PDF/print. These need verification, not assumption.

## Strategic direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

**This is a RECONCILIATION wave, not a build wave.** The system is alive and governing; the ledger is stale. The finished experience: the epic anchor either closed with every criterion stamped `met: true` + file:line + PR evidence, or carrying exactly the honest remainder — and nothing in between.

Three streams, in lean order:

1. **Evidence the 4 anchor criteria.** Each criterion gets concrete file:line + PR/CI proof (manifest single-source, four surface-families adopted, drift gate green in CI, styleguides ratified). If any criterion cannot be evidenced, that IS the wave's work.
2. **Triage the 23 open children into three bins:** (i) *shipped elsewhere* — close with evidence pointing at the PR that shipped it (the PortableDoc showcase, TUI creative slates, and studio-ui-premium epics plausibly absorbed much of W5.B); (ii) *obsolete/superseded* — close as cut with one-line rationale; (iii) *genuinely open* — keep, and decide whether it blocks epic-close or moves to a small named successor task (the epic must not stay open as a component-block wishlist).
3. **Verify the outside-candidates.** Email, /activate CP page, marketing/docs site, PDF/print: for each, either prove it draws from the lockstep (or is out of the anchor's scope with a written rationale) or cut ONE smallest slice through the same manifest. Suspected true gaps: **email** (not in the 17-artifact list) and possibly `--color-graph-canvas` (open child `au-w3-graph-canvas-token`).

**Leaning:** (a)-with-a-small-(b) — stamp and close the anchor this wave, with at most 1-3 surgical build slices (email tokens, graph-canvas token, pdrender-open-task reconciliation) if the verifiers prove real gaps. Tree-tidiness earns nothing; honest evidence earns everything.

## Survey plan (15 surveyors, in flight)

| # | Key | Question | Why it changes the plan |
|---|-----|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | lockstep-inventory | Map each of the 17 emit artifacts to its output file path and the product surface that consumes it; run check.mjs and report every part's status | This is the coverage baseline the close-or-cut decision rests on |
| 2 | epic-children-triage | Full state of all 55 children; briefs of the 23 open ones | The triage bins can't be designed without the briefs |
| 3 | paper-components-reality | Did the W5.B blocks (hero…chart) + W5.D gallery actually ship? file:line + PR | Decides whether ~14 open tasks close-with-evidence or stay |
| 4 | email-surface | Do the 14 transactional email types draw from generated tokens? | Email is the strongest candidate for a genuine gap |
| 5 | cp-activate-login | Are /activate + CP login pages styled from the lockstep (cloud SPA artifact)? | Named candidate in the wish |
| 6 | marketing-docs-site | Does an in-repo marketing/docs site exist, and is it token-fed? | Named candidate; may be out-of-scope by anchor wording |
| 7 | pdf-print | Any PDF/print export path and is it tokenized? | Named candidate; likely scope-cut with rationale |
| 8 | anchor-criteria-evidence | Concrete file:line + PR/CI evidence for each of the 4 criteria | The close needs stamps, not vibes |
| 9 | styleguide-ratified | Which per-surface styleguides exist and render from real tokens? | Criterion 4 hinges on this |
| 10 | drift-gate-ci | Is check.mjs (incl. Part F + H) + studio-literal-check actually wired into CI and green on HEAD? | Criterion 3 hinges on this |
| 11 | literal-color-residue | Raw-color leak size per surface outside generated files + exemptions | Distinguishes "unified" from "unified-ish" |
| 12 | brand-mark-favicon | State of marks/favicons across surfaces (open W6.16) | Decides if W6.16 is real remaining work or cut |
| 13 | prior-papers | Prior aesthetic/unified-aesthetic/studio-ui-premium papers: what did they promise as remaining? | Avoids re-deciding what a past wave already decided |
| 14 | graph-canvas-token | Does --color-graph-canvas exist? Is the graph surface hardcoded dark? | Smallest plausible build slice |
| 15 | pdrender-token-truth | Reconcile: au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens open vs "Go pdrender ok" in emit --check | A ledger/reality contradiction that must not survive the wave |

## Ledger links

- Epic anchor: task `aesthetic-unification-epic` (this Paper's id is stamped on its `wave_paper` field; `wave_status` = surveying).
- Slice tasks: filed at Decide; each will carry this Paper's id.

---
*Appended by later phases: Survey digest + verify plan (Digest) → decisions + wave plan (Decide) → debrief (Review).*


---

## Digest (2026-07-11) — survey folded, verify fleet in flight

**Wave status: VERIFYING** — 8 targeted verifiers launched (plan below). Decide follows their proofs.

### What 15 surveyors established

**1. The lockstep is proven green, twice over.** `node design/emit.mjs --check` = all 17 artifacts in sync; `node design/check.mjs` = Parts A–H PASS (Part F theme-compiler byte-identity, Part H 162/162 WCAG-AA), run live by two independent surveyors AND confirmed in the real CI log (doc-gates run 29128797161 on HEAD 91531b27). Full artifact→consumer map is now on record (survey `lockstep-inventory`).

**2. The wish's four candidate gap surfaces mostly dissolved on contact:**
- **Email — NOT a gap.** The "14 GUI-premium email types" are the 14 PortableDoc fleet block types rendered `:email` for the mailed-paper view, and they draw through `Palettes.email_skin → TokensGen` = artifact #11/17 (`api/lib/barkpark/portable_doc/render/tokens_gen.ex`, generated from tokens.json `paperEmail`). One documented literal exception (terminal traffic-dots, `panels_email.ex:104-106`, charter D4). Role tones ride `design/status-manifest.json` (a governed sibling manifest — evidence wording must say "tokens.json + status-manifest.json", not "tokens.json alone"). Transactional emails (reset/invite/digest) are plain text — no aesthetic surface at all.
- **/activate + CP login — NOT a gap.** All CP routes (`/`, `/dashboard`, `/new`, `/activate`) serve one SPA (`router.ex:317-348` → `index.html:14` → `app.css`), and `app.css` IS the "cloud SPA" lockstep artifact (emit.mjs:1720). Login/signup are JS modes of the same screen.
- **Marketing/docs site — scope-cut.** barkpark.cloud is served by web/ (in lockstep as "web demo" + "web TS tokens"). `js/docs/` (Fumadocs) is genuinely outside the lockstep but is a known-dormant, unwired, undeployed app — pre-existing decision record at `docs/decisions/deferred.md:8`. Tokenizing an unserved site earns nothing.
- **PDF/print — scope-cut.** No PDF pipeline exists anywhere (repo-wide grep clean). Print = tokenized `@media print` blocks in both reader layouts (`sheets.html.heex:261-277`, `bulldocs.html.heex:838-878`) with exactly one frozen paper-white literal each (exemptions.json:13, PR #2273).

**3. Real gaps surfaced where nobody guessed:**
- **Literal-color residue (contests criterion 1).** Using check.mjs Part E's own counting rule: ~880 un-ledgered literal hits across ~104 files beyond the 4 frozen exemption files. Top offenders: `api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css` 181 (dead `var(--paper-x, #hex)` fallbacks — the exact anti-pattern the root.html.heex sweep purged) + its web mirror 107; `bp-graph.js` byte-identical pair 91×2 (hand-authored Canvas2D palette, zero token consumption); `paper-surface.css` 51 (the source-of-truth file itself is never counted anywhere); `tickets/inbox_live.ex` 48; `tasks/web/board_live.ex` 32 (raw unwrapped hex, no var() at all); `sheets.html.heex` 31 (a THIRD independent hand-set `--paper-*` block). Raw tally includes test-fixture/generated noise — needs a judgment pass before it decides C1.
- **web portable-doc.tsx (the real half of `au-w5-pdrender-web-tokens`).** The live /papers+post web reader hand-codes callout tones as a literal Tailwind palette map (`portable-doc.tsx:256-266`) with no relationship to tokens.json — a parallel color system on a flagship surface. The Go pdrender half of the same task is DONE, shipped under theme-system PRs #1395/#1691/#1984; criterion wording "via semrole" is architecturally false by design (pdrender may never import semrole; it gets a byte-identical emitted copy).
- **Graph-canvas token** (`au-w3-graph-canvas-token`) — confirmed real, small, self-documented at `graph-landing.tsx:56`. The Studio Canvas2D graph (bp-graph.js) is a separate, bigger problem and NOT in that task's scope.
- **Brand mark (`au-w6-brand-mark`) — genuine and unabsorbed.** No logo asset exists anywhere; three surfaces brand three ways; favicons diverge (web = real ICO, api = 152-byte PNG mislabeled .ico, cloud = NONE). Needs a human-drawn mark + sign-off — wrong shape for a surgical slice; spin-off candidate (with a possible tiny "one favicon everywhere" mechanical sub-slice).

**4. Anchor criteria honest state:** C1 contested by the residue finding (stampable only with an exemptions-extension or fix slices — verifier decides which). C2 met with the documented email nuance (brand/rule hex deliberately pinned to email-golden, tokens_gen.ex:11-14 says "w3 reconciles the two" — did w3 run? unverified). C3 green-on-every-run but NOT GitHub-enforced (branch protection 404; rulesets API not yet queried — evidence must say "blocking CI step, team-enforced" unless rulesets says otherwise). C4 SPLIT: per-surface styleguides real (web type ladder still a hand-kept preview, W3.9 unwired), the one true cross-surface instrument (`__preview__/coherence.html`, token-real, test-covered) is UNROUTED, and the ratification EVENT (au-w6-visual-audit, the charter's S11 exit gate) never happened. C4 cannot be stamped met:true today.

**5. Children triage ground truth (kills a strategist hypothesis).** The lean "studio-ui-premium plausibly absorbed W5.B" is FALSE. The 11 `au-w5-comp-*` + `au-w5-paper-components-view` were fabricated-done (identical boilerplate, null claim) and reopened 2026-07-08; the blocks (hero…sparkline) do not exist in compose.ex's ~50-type registry; issue #1475 open, no PR anywhere. All 12 tasks STILL carry the fabricated `outcome.summary` — dangling false claims needing cleanup regardless of build-or-cut. The epic's real charter (`.claude/workflows/bp-unified-aesthetic-endgame-charter.md`) never scoped W5.B/W6 at all — its own remainder is only S10 (literal ratchet) + S11 (sign-off). Also: studio-ui-premium epic is actually still OPEN (3/4 criteria, human re-verdict pending), contrary to the strategize framing. One intra-survey contradiction to settle: `epic-children-triage` calls `au-w5-comp-chart` evidence-closeable (chart_html exists); `paper-components-reality` says that chart infra is PRE-EXISTING dataviz, not the task's deliverable.

### Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

- No marketing site besides web/; no PDF pipeline; no logo/mark asset repo-wide; no graph token in tokens.json/emit/check; no ratification record in docs/decisions or docs/cards; no branch protection on main; no Barkpark Papers for the epic's W1–W4 history (the git-committed charter .md is the true memory); no dedicated email ARTIFACT entry (coverage is transitive via artifact #11); no W5.B block code under ANY name in api/lib.
- **Corners no surveyor reached:** GitHub rulesets API (newer than branch protection); `cards_email.ex` never hex-grepped (siblings were); a PR-event doc-gates run (only push runs checked); whether "w3 reconciles the two" ever ran; the 14 email template OUTPUTS not enumerated; emit.mjs builder bodies lines ~922-1820 read only via the byte-parity gate; CLI `about` banner for brand criterion; `bp search query` prior-art sweep (early surveyors used a wrong verb — the working incantation is `bp search query "<q>"`).

### Verify plan — 8 assignments, in flight now

| # | Key | Model | Question (compressed) | Proof to RUN |
|---|-----|-------|----------------------|--------------|
| 1 | residue-c1-verdict | opus | Classify the ~880 un-ledgered literals (noise / email-safe / real residue); per-file verdict for the 7 top offenders + figures.ex; can C1 be stamped with an exemptions extension, or does it need slices first? | node design/check.mjs && node design/emit.mjs --check; replicate Part E count on named files |
| 2 | ci-enforcement-c3 | sonnet | Do GitHub rulesets (not classic protection) require doc-gates? Are PR-event runs green? Final C3 evidence wording. | gh api rulesets; gh run list --event pull_request |

**Wave status: COMPLETE.** All 3 slices built green, adversarially reviewed, ZERO code fixes needed. Grade: **A-**.

Inbox becomes theme-aware for the first time (light users see light — deliberate pixel change). .ex → waits for Elixir Test CI on the PR. |

# Authoring Excellence — Wave 4: Seal the Last Bypass

*Living wave paper. Opened at Strategize (2026-07-13). Every later phase appends here — Digest folds the survey, Decide records the wave plan, Review closes the story. Workers never write this paper; they write their own bp task.*

Epic: `authoring-excellence` · Charter: `.claude/workflows/bp-authoring-excellence-charter.md` (authoritative over the design paper). Prior waves: `authoring-excellence-wave-2026-07-10` (wall built), `…-2026-07-12` (D10 window closed, search payoff), `…-2026-07-12b` (feedback rings, D26–D32 ratified).

---

## The wish

> Seal the **LAST** publish-wall bypass. PRIMARY slice `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (D23 blockers a/b/c, D13 fifth mount) — a ~80%-complete `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall` extraction **already exists** in the preserved worktree `.claude/worktrees/wf_3df713cf-2a1-28` (force-terminated mid-gate). The builder **resumes** that WIP, not restart. Then fold in the carried W4 findings: verify D28 recompute-else-drop landed (#2817) and close the loop; exemption-cleared-before-E3 telemetry; `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss`; `ae-caller-error-surfacing` residue. Weight **finishing** journeys over net-new. Every published doc/task this wave carries registered weighted tags per the wall.

North star (charter): *a document is well-labeled iff search finds it. Drafts stay free; publish is the wall.* The wall is mounted at four seams — core `lifecycle.ex` publishes (papers + tasks). The FIFTH seam, `BlockOps.upsert_paper`, births **published** papers via direct Repo writes and structurally cannot route through `publish_document`. It is the one door left open. This wave closes it.

---

## What actually landed vs the ledger (reconciliation — read this first)

Two ledger claims did not survive contact with `main`. The wave is shaped by fixing them honestly.

**FINDING 1 — D28 is NOT on main (false-done).** The ledger marks `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` **done (6/6)** and the charter wave-2 review cites #2817 as merged. But:

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor d343c793 HEAD` → **NOT in main**. Commit #2817 exists, but lives only on unrelated branches (`loop-epic/…chat…`, `omx/task…`) — it was **never merged to main**.
- `main`'s `lifecycle.ex:257-264` still carries the OLD `stamp_main_tag`: `:error -> content` (passthrough, NOT `Map.delete`).
- `main`'s `lifecycle.ex:236` still clears the exemption at **spine-pass**, before E3/E4 run.
- No `wall_rejection` telemetry exists anywhere in `main`.

So **all three** D28 payloads — recompute-else-drop, exemption-after-full-wall, first wall telemetry — are absent from main. The ledger is lying about ratchet-telemetry.

**The silver lining:** the preserved worktree's `authoring_wall.ex` **already folds the fixed D28 semantics into the extraction** — its `enforce/5` clears the exemption only on a full pass (`if exempt? and spine_passed?`) and `stamp_main_tag/2` is recompute-else-drop. So **landing the extraction lands D28 correctly, at the one shared chokepoint.** The tentative ruling below makes the extraction the honest D28 landing and reopens the ratchet-telemetry ledger.

**FINDING 2 — `ae-caller-error-surfacing` (D23) IS on main (the lead's note is stale).** #2793 (`900981af`) merged; `adopt.ex` carries the `collapse` field + `{:ok, doc, collapse}`, `link.ex` logs, valueref gained the `publish_failed` clause, Studio drains advisories. The lead's "github adopt/link + valueref still swallow wall errors" is a **stale carry** from before #2793. Survey confirms the residue (if any) but this is largely a no-op — down-weighted.

**FINDING 3 — the worktree is 100 commits behind main and its diff is contaminated.** `git diff main --stat` from the worktree shows deletions of `bp-chat-tui-charter.md` (−81), `bp-hyperquiz-charter.md` (−53), `listen_controller.ex` (−85), `listen_backpressure_test.exs` (−174), `chat_transcript_window_test.exs` (−99), `rate_limit_test.exs`. **These are not extraction work** — they are reversions of post-fork main work the stale base never saw. The builder MUST rebase onto current main and keep ONLY the genuine extraction files (see Direction).

---

## Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

**The finished experience.** Barkpark has exactly ONE fail-closed door for every published paper and task — whether born through `lifecycle.publish_document` (autosave, patch, task publish) or through `BlockOps.upsert_paper` (bulldocs ingest, studio_chat plan_papers, canvas). Both run the same `AuthoringWall.enforce` chain, return byte-identical tuples, and stamp `main_tag` the same way. An ingest POST with weighted tags passes; a tag-less or unknown-tag POST gets a specific, retryable 422/409 — not a hint-less `invalid_paper`. The ratchet is honest: a grandfathered doc that fails a LATER gate keeps its grandfathering, and no republish ever carries a stale `main_tag`. The wall's first rejection telemetry makes a `label_spine` 422 distinguishable from any other 422 in prod logs. There is no fifth bypass left.

**Priorities, finishing over net-new:**

1. **PRIMARY — `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (opus, RESUME).** Resume the extraction from `.claude/worktrees/wf_3df713cf-2a1-28`. First act: **rebase onto current main and isolate to extraction files only** (`authoring_wall.ex`, `lifecycle.ex`, `content.ex`, `papers.ex`, `block_ops.ex`, `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex`, `plan_papers.ex`, `label_fixtures.ex`, seed fixtures, the two new test files) — discard the contamination reversions. Then finish per D26/D27/D28: `enforce/5` shared chain, `upsert_paper(attrs, opts \\\\ [])` default-arg on **all three** delegations (content.ex / papers.ex / block_ops.ex — miss one and the bypass silently dies), enforcement ON by default, self-id ref so a paper can't near-duplicate itself, ingest attrs gain `tags`/`description` passthrough, plan_papers = `bypass_wall: true` (D23-b), the 13-caller audit (real labels or grep-able `bypass_wall: true` + one-line rationale), LabelFixtures paper-attrs wrapper + the ~288-fixture mechanical sweep. Gate green in the worktree, then hand merge to the lead.

2. **D28 reconciliation (folded into the primary, not a separate build).** Because the extraction rewrites the whole chain into `AuthoringWall`, landing #2817 separately first would only create a conflict the extraction discards. Tentative ruling: **the extraction IS the honest D28 landing.** The primary slice must carry the D28 red-proof tests (recompute-else-drop; exemption survives a failed weighted adoption; wall-rejection telemetry at all three sites) so main gains D28 for the first time. Reopen `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` honestly, close it only when the extraction proves D28 on main. Decide confirms whether this folds cleanly or needs a tiny separate lifecycle slice first.

3. **`ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` (small, opus).** Known fix shape (charter backlog D25): `ensure_map/1` gains a `when is_binary(s), do: %{"tag" => s}` head + a protective test — read side already proven tolerant. Independent of the Elixir wall gate's timing; can build in parallel. Survey must first pin the real `paper_field_block.ex` path (the charter's guessed path missed).

4. **`ae-ingest-honest-errors` (D27) — likely folded into the primary.** The worktree already touches `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex`. D27 wants three per-tuple case heads (`label_spine`→422, `unknown_tag`→422, `duplicate_of`→409) via `render_error`→`Errors.to_envelope`, keeping `invalid_paper`/`halted`/`malformed` byte-identical. Survey maps whether the worktree already did this or it needs a split-out opus slice.

**Model constraint (hard this wave):** Fable is exhausted. Every builder is **opus**. The primary was "large, fable" in the roadmap — but the WIP is 80% done and the spec is exhaustively pinned by D26/D27/D28, so a well-specified opus resume is tractable. If Decide judges it too big for one opus pass, **decompose** into fully-specified opus slices (e.g. split the mechanical fixture sweep from the core extraction) — never reach for fable. Verify fleet: opus for judgment digs, sonnet only for breadth mapping.

**Where the Kinsta/Vercel bar is not yet met:** a bulldocs ingest that drops `tags` and collapses every failure to a hint-less `invalid_paper` is the opposite of the quality bar — an agent gets no machine-readable retry. Closing that (tags passthrough + specific errors) is the wave's quality payoff, not just the mount.

---

## Survey plan (cast wide — Digest distills)

Every assignment below becomes one Sonnet surveyor unless marked opus. Width is cheap now.

*(the surveyor questions are enumerated in the workflow's survey field; this section is appended by Digest with the returned answers)*

---

*Status: SURVEYING. Next: Digest folds the survey + names the verify fleet before verifiers fly.*


---

# DIGEST — survey folded, verify fleet named (2026-07-13)

## The pivotal correction: the survey baselines were read against a STALE local checkout

The Strategize brief's headline finding — "#2817 (D28 ratchet honesty + telemetry) is FALSE-DONE, absent from main" — **does not survive contact with origin/main.** Digest re-ran the ancestry against the fetched remote:

- **Local `main` (16e259ee) is 100 commits BEHIND origin/main (7e037ca1) and 25 ahead** — a two-way divergence, never pulled. Every surveyor who "read main" read the stale local tree.
- **#2817 (d343c793, D28) IS an ancestor of origin/main; NOT of local HEAD.** On origin/main, `lifecycle.ex` already carries recompute-else-drop (`Map.delete(content,"main_tag")` at :308), clear-only-after-full-wall (`if validated? and exempt?` at :143), and **`emit_wall_rejection/3` telemetry firing `[:barkpark,:authoring,:wall_rejection]` at all three rejection sites** (:234/:238/:242) with a red-proof test in `lifecycle_test.exs:486-507`.
- **#2818 (f1fc2832, D27) IS on origin/main too** — `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` already has the three specific error heads (label_spine 422 / unknown_tag 422 / duplicate_of 409) via `render_error/2`, sitting ABOVE the `invalid_paper` catch-all (:131-138, :187-194).

## Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

**The finished experience.** Barkpark has exactly ONE fail-closed door for every published paper and task — whether born through `lifecycle.publish_document` (autosave, patch, task publish) or through `BlockOps.upsert_paper` (bulldocs ingest, studio_chat plan_papers, canvas). Both run the same `AuthoringWall.enforce` chain, return byte-identical tuples, and stamp `main_tag` the same way. An ingest POST with weighted tags passes; a tag-less or unknown-tag POST gets a specific, retryable 422/409 — not a hint-less `invalid_paper`. The ratchet is honest: a grandfathered doc that fails a LATER gate keeps its grandfathering, and no republish ever carries a stale `main_tag`. The wall's first rejection telemetry makes a `label_spine` 422 distinguishable from any other 422 in prod logs. There is no fifth bypass left.

| Fixture sweep (40 files/114 callsites) | `ae-fixture-sweep` | Elixir test fixtures | opus | medium | `cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test` on the 40 swept files (branch from the core; mount must be present) |
| Editor legacy-tag write-loss | `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` | Studio LiveView (paper_field_block.ex) | opus | small | `cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test <new paper_editor test>` |

Backlog filed this wave: `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` (D36). Still open: `ae-curator-feed`, `ae-dedup-trgm-index`, `ae-paper-decision-sync`.

*Status: BUILDING. The core is a RESUME — the builder continues the preserved worktree's WIP reconciled onto origin/main, does not restart. Review closes this story.*


---

# REVIEW — the last bypass sealed (wave 4 complete, 2026-07-13)

*Reviewer (Fable), last hands before merge. Reviewed all 3 green slices end-to-end, fixed one cross-slice break in place, re-ran every gate on the true integrated tree. **Grade: A-.***

## What shipped (per slice, integration-ordered core → sweep → editor)

**S1 — `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (core).** Final branch `loop-epic/seal-the-last-wall-bypass-authoringwall--0-r`. `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall.enforce/5` is now the ONE shared chain: exemption-read-once → label spine → E3 registry → E4 dedup → clear-on-FULL-pass → main_tag stamp. `Lifecycle.publish_document` delegates byte-identically (its 225-line inline chain is gone). `BlockOps.upsert_paper` mounts the same chain on a synthesized `%Document{}` ref (doc_id = slug) BEFORE the Repo write — the self-id reaches DedupWall's incumbent exclusion so a paper can never near-duplicate itself. D34 reconciliation verified clean: telemetry CARRIED into `enforce`'s else-seam (the `[:barkpark,:authoring,:wall_rejection]` event + `Logger.warning` fire live in the gate run for all three codes), #2818 render_error heads preserved, D26 tags/description passthrough added to both ingest attrs whitelists, the 3 D27 skips activated, the ingest_wall tagless assertion upgraded to `code=label_spine`. `opts \\ []` threaded through ALL three delegations (content.ex / papers.ex / block_ops.ex). Caller audit complete: 2 ingest heads ENFORCE, plan_papers + seeds/clean + 4 priv seeds carry `bypass_wall: true` + a grep-able rationale. **Gate 65/0.** The mount test is genuinely non-vacuous — verified `write_encrypted_paper` seeds `base_content` from the existing row, so the recompute-else-drop test's stale `main_tag` is really present and really dropped. One deliberate improvement over the pre-extraction behavior: `stamp_main_tag/2` scopes recompute-else-drop to `@walled_types`, so a non-walled type now keeps a user field named `main_tag` instead of having it silently eaten.

**S2 — `ae-fixture-sweep`.** Final branch `loop-epic/fixture-sweep-wrap-40-test-files-114-ups-1-r` (= core + sweep, stacked). 114 callsites across 40 files wrapped in `LabelFixtures.paper_attrs/1`; 2 callsites needed semantic hand-edits (content_projection_test, sharing_composition_p4_test's ingest POST). **Stacked gate 499/0 across all 40 files.** Completeness PROVEN, not asserted: the set-difference of {every test file referencing `upsert_paper`} minus {files touched by any slice} is EMPTY (44 files, all covered). The single ingest-referencing file not touched (`capabilities_project_test`) is a capability-tier visibility test, not a paper birth. No uncovered wall-facing path remains.

**S3 — `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss`.** Final branch `loop-epic/paperfieldblock-composite-editor-must-no-2-r` (= core + editor + reviewer fix). Two seams: a RENDER seam (`normalize_legacy_composite_rows`, SCOPED to composites that declare a `"tag"` subfield) reconstitutes a legacy bare-string row to `%{"tag"=>s}` before the editor renders it; plus the charter-mandated generic `ensure_map` `is_binary` merge head as belt-and-suspenders. The protective test reds without the fix and greens with it; two genericity-guard tests pin a non-tag composite (amount/currency) and a scalar arrayOf (keywords) round-tripping unharmed with NO spurious `tag` key. **Directory gate 103/0 on the integration.**

## What the reviewer fixed in place (the one real blemish)

The editor slice was filed "independent, parallel-safe" — it is NOT. Its seed helpers, and the shared `PaperEditorTestHelpers` it `use`s (which the sweep wrapped), birth papers through bare `upsert_paper` with no tags. The merged wall 422s those births. The slice's declared gate (`mix test .../paper_editor/`) passed ONLY because it ran on the editor's own branch WITHOUT the wall present — a textbook vacuous green (the right thing did not produce the pass). Re-run on the true integrated tree, the editor test reds 3/3 with `{:label_spine, field: "description"}`. **Reviewer fix:** `bypass_wall: true` on the 3 seed helpers (editor-mechanics fixtures, wall not under test, bypass keeps the seeded blocks pristine for the exact-HTML render + round-trip assertions). Committed on the editor -r branch; integrated gate now 103/0.

## Cross-slice reality the lead MUST honor

These are ONE integrated unit, not three independent merges. Because D35 split the mount (breaks ~288 fixtures) from the sweep (repairs them), **a core-only PR REDS the full Elixir Test gate.** Merge order MUST be core → sweep → editor, stacked. All three -r branches carry the single core commit (git dedupes on merge); the slice file sets are disjoint; the full gate is green only on the combined tip. The editor slice depends on BOTH core (for `bypass_wall/2` to compile) AND sweep (for the shared helper wrap). Confidence net beyond the slice gates: content+papers dirs 829/0; web-controllers+studio 2154/1, where the 1 is the documented studio-chat async sandbox-ownership flake (`chat_live_test` passes 274/0 in isolation, unrelated to the wall).

## Ledger audit

Honest across all three tasks: each `in_progress`, every built criterion stamped `met` with evidence as the work happened, the merge-gated criterion left `met=false` for the lead to close on merge. No lies or omissions to correct. The reviewer's editor-seed fix is recorded here and in the charter wave log, not as a criterion flip.

## Grade: A-

The wave FINISHES the epic's central promise — one fail-closed door for every published paper and task, the last bypass sealed — with high correctness and PROVEN completeness (the sweep's coverage is a set-difference, not a claim), and it REDUCES duplication (a shared chokepoint replaces two forked chains). The single deduction is the editor slice's vacuous green: its gate passed pre-integration and would have reddened the merge, requiring reviewer intervention to catch — exactly the distrust-vacuous-green lesson the charter carries. The delivered, fixed, integrated result is excellent.

*Status: COMPLETE. The wall is mounted at all FIVE seams. Remaining epic work is backlog observability + doc-truth (see the charter wave log), none blocking the north star.*</article>

# Authoring Excellence — Wave 4: Seal the Last Bypass

*Living wave paper. Opened at Strategize (2026-07-13). Every later phase appends here — Digest folds the survey, Decide records the wave plan, Review closes the story. Workers never write this paper; they write their own bp task.*

Epic: `authoring-excellence` · Charter: `.claude/workflows/bp-authoring-excellence-charter.md` (authoritative over the design paper). Prior waves: `authoring-excellence-wave-2026-07-10` (wall built), `…-2026-07-12` (D10 window closed, search payoff), `…-2026-07-12b` (feedback rings, D26–D32 ratified).

---

## The wish

> Seal the **LAST** publish-wall bypass. PRIMARY slice `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (D23 blockers a/b/c, D13 fifth mount) — a ~80%-complete `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall` extraction **already exists** in the preserved worktree `.claude/worktrees/wf_3df713cf-2a1-28` (force-terminated mid-gate). The builder **resumes** that WIP, not restart. Then fold in the carried W4 findings: verify D28 recompute-else-drop landed (#2817) and close the loop; exemption-cleared-before-E3 telemetry; `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss`; `ae-caller-error-surfacing` residue. Weight **finishing** journeys over net-new. Every published doc/task this wave carries registered weighted tags per the wall.

North star (charter): *a document is well-labeled iff search finds it. Drafts stay free; publish is the wall.* The wall is mounted at four seams — core `lifecycle.ex` publishes (papers + tasks). The FIFTH seam, `BlockOps.upsert_paper`, births **published** papers via direct Repo writes and structurally cannot route through `publish_document`. It is the one door left open. This wave closes it.

---

## What actually landed vs the ledger (reconciliation — read this first)

Two ledger claims did not survive contact with `main`. The wave is shaped by fixing them honestly.

**FINDING 1 — D28 is NOT on main (false-done).** The ledger marks `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` **done (6/6)** and the charter wave-2 review cites #2817 as merged. But:

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor d343c793 HEAD` → **NOT in main**. Commit #2817 exists, but lives only on unrelated branches (`loop-epic/…chat…`, `omx/task…`) — it was **never merged to main**.
- `main`'s `lifecycle.ex:257-264` still carries the OLD `stamp_main_tag`: `:error -> content` (passthrough, NOT `Map.delete`).
- `main`'s `lifecycle.ex:236` still clears the exemption at **spine-pass**, before E3/E4 run.
- No `wall_rejection` telemetry exists anywhere in `main`.

So **all three** D28 payloads — recompute-else-drop, exemption-after-full-wall, first wall telemetry — are absent from main. The ledger is lying about ratchet-telemetry.

**The silver lining:** the preserved worktree's `authoring_wall.ex` **already folds the fixed D28 semantics into the extraction** — its `enforce/5` clears the exemption only on a full pass (`if exempt? and spine_passed?`) and `stamp_main_tag/2` is recompute-else-drop. So **landing the extraction lands D28 correctly, at the one shared chokepoint.** The tentative ruling below makes the extraction the honest D28 landing and reopens the ratchet-telemetry ledger.

**FINDING 2 — `ae-caller-error-surfacing` (D23) IS on main (the lead's note is stale).** #2793 (`900981af`) merged; `adopt.ex` carries the `collapse` field + `{:ok, doc, collapse}`, `link.ex` logs, valueref gained the `publish_failed` clause, Studio drains advisories. The lead's "github adopt/link + valueref still swallow wall errors" is a **stale carry** from before #2793. Survey confirms the residue (if any) but this is largely a no-op — down-weighted.

**FINDING 3 — the worktree is 100 commits behind main and its diff is contaminated.** `git diff main --stat` from the worktree shows deletions of `bp-chat-tui-charter.md` (−81), `bp-hyperquiz-charter.md` (−53), `listen_controller.ex` (−85), `listen_backpressure_test.exs` (−174), `chat_transcript_window_test.exs` (−99), `rate_limit_test.exs`. **These are not extraction work** — they are reversions of post-fork main work the stale base never saw. The builder MUST rebase onto current main and keep ONLY the genuine extraction files (see Direction).

---

## Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

**The finished experience.** Barkpark has exactly ONE fail-closed door for every published paper and task — whether born through `lifecycle.publish_document` (autosave, patch, task publish) or through `BlockOps.upsert_paper` (bulldocs ingest, studio_chat plan_papers, canvas). Both run the same `AuthoringWall.enforce` chain, return byte-identical tuples, and stamp `main_tag` the same way. An ingest POST with weighted tags passes; a tag-less or unknown-tag POST gets a specific, retryable 422/409 — not a hint-less `invalid_paper`. The ratchet is honest: a grandfathered doc that fails a LATER gate keeps its grandfathering, and no republish ever carries a stale `main_tag`. The wall's first rejection telemetry makes a `label_spine` 422 distinguishable from any other 422 in prod logs. There is no fifth bypass left.

**Priorities, finishing over net-new:**

1. **PRIMARY — `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (opus, RESUME).** Resume the extraction from `.claude/worktrees/wf_3df713cf-2a1-28`. First act: **rebase onto current main and isolate to extraction files only** (`authoring_wall.ex`, `lifecycle.ex`, `content.ex`, `papers.ex`, `block_ops.ex`, `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex`, `plan_papers.ex`, `label_fixtures.ex`, seed fixtures, the two new test files) — discard the contamination reversions. Then finish per D26/D27/D28: `enforce/5` shared chain, `upsert_paper(attrs, opts \\\\ [])` default-arg on **all three** delegations (content.ex / papers.ex / block_ops.ex — miss one and the bypass silently dies), enforcement ON by default, self-id ref so a paper can't near-duplicate itself, ingest attrs gain `tags`/`description` passthrough, plan_papers = `bypass_wall: true` (D23-b), the 13-caller audit (real labels or grep-able `bypass_wall: true` + one-line rationale), LabelFixtures paper-attrs wrapper + the ~288-fixture mechanical sweep. Gate green in the worktree, then hand merge to the lead.

2. **D28 reconciliation (folded into the primary, not a separate build).** Because the extraction rewrites the whole chain into `AuthoringWall`, landing #2817 separately first would only create a conflict the extraction discards. Tentative ruling: **the extraction IS the honest D28 landing.** The primary slice must carry the D28 red-proof tests (recompute-else-drop; exemption survives a failed weighted adoption; wall-rejection telemetry at all three sites) so main gains D28 for the first time. Reopen `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` honestly, close it only when the extraction proves D28 on main. Decide confirms whether this folds cleanly or needs a tiny separate lifecycle slice first.

3. **`ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` (small, opus).** Known fix shape (charter backlog D25): `ensure_map/1` gains a `when is_binary(s), do: %{"tag" => s}` head + a protective test — read side already proven tolerant. Independent of the Elixir wall gate's timing; can build in parallel. Survey must first pin the real `paper_field_block.ex` path (the charter's guessed path missed).

4. **`ae-ingest-honest-errors` (D27) — likely folded into the primary.** The worktree already touches `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex`. D27 wants three per-tuple case heads (`label_spine`→422, `unknown_tag`→422, `duplicate_of`→409) via `render_error`→`Errors.to_envelope`, keeping `invalid_paper`/`halted`/`malformed` byte-identical. Survey maps whether the worktree already did this or it needs a split-out opus slice.

**Model constraint (hard this wave):** Fable is exhausted. Every builder is **opus**. The primary was "large, fable" in the roadmap — but the WIP is 80% done and the spec is exhaustively pinned by D26/D27/D28, so a well-specified opus resume is tractable. If Decide judges it too big for one opus pass, **decompose** into fully-specified opus slices (e.g. split the mechanical fixture sweep from the core extraction) — never reach for fable. Verify fleet: opus for judgment digs, sonnet only for breadth mapping.

**Where the Kinsta/Vercel bar is not yet met:** a bulldocs ingest that drops `tags` and collapses every failure to a hint-less `invalid_paper` is the opposite of the quality bar — an agent gets no machine-readable retry. Closing that (tags passthrough + specific errors) is the wave's quality payoff, not just the mount.

---

## Survey plan (cast wide — Digest distills)

Every assignment below becomes one Sonnet surveyor unless marked opus. Width is cheap now.

*(the surveyor questions are enumerated in the workflow's survey field; this section is appended by Digest with the returned answers)*

---

*Status: SURVEYING. Next: Digest folds the survey + names the verify fleet before verifiers fly.*


---

# DIGEST — survey folded, verify fleet named (2026-07-13)

## The pivotal correction: the survey baselines were read against a STALE local checkout

The Strategize brief's headline finding — "#2817 (D28 ratchet honesty + telemetry) is FALSE-DONE, absent from main" — **does not survive contact with origin/main.** Digest re-ran the ancestry against the fetched remote:

- **Local `main` (16e259ee) is 100 commits BEHIND origin/main (7e037ca1) and 25 ahead** — a two-way divergence, never pulled. Every surveyor who "read main" read the stale local tree.
- **#2817 (d343c793, D28) IS an ancestor of origin/main; NOT of local HEAD.** On origin/main, `lifecycle.ex` already carries recompute-else-drop (`Map.delete(content,"main_tag")` at :308), clear-only-after-full-wall (`if validated? and exempt?` at :143), and **`emit_wall_rejection/3` telemetry firing `[:barkpark,:authoring,:wall_rejection]` at all three rejection sites** (:234/:238/:242) with a red-proof test in `lifecycle_test.exs:486-507`.
- **#2818 (f1fc2832, D27) IS on origin/main too** — `bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex` already has the three specific error heads (label_spine 422 / unknown_tag 422 / duplicate_of 409) via `render_error/2`, sitting ABOVE the `invalid_paper` catch-all (:131-138, :187-194).
- **#2793 (900981af, caller-error-surfacing) IS on origin/main** — github adopt/link + valueref no longer swallow wall errors. Verify-only, genuinely landed.
- **The shared `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall` module is ABSENT from origin/main** — D27/D28 landed *inline* in lifecycle.ex + the ingest controller, NOT via a shared chokepoint. That extraction is the one genuinely-unbuilt thing.
- **`ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` is CLOSED in the ledger** (lead-fable, epoch 8, 2026-07-13) and is *correctly* closed — it landed via #2817. **Reopening it would itself be a false claim. DO NOT reopen it.**

## What this does to the wave shape

The preserved worktree forked at **99eb9583 = only 25 commits behind origin/main** (the "100 behind" everywhere in the survey is distance behind the *stale local* main). The fork **predates #2817 and #2818** — both landed in that 25-commit gap. So the worktree's WIP was built against a pre-fix lifecycle.ex/ingest-controller and independently re-derived the D28 ratchet semantics into its `authoring_wall.ex` — **but it has ZERO telemetry** (confirmed: no `wall_rejection`/Logger anywhere in the module) and its ingest-controller change is **only the D26 tags/description passthrough** (:98-99, :148-149), NOT the error heads.

**The primary slice is therefore a RECONCILIATION, not a fresh build:**
1. Fresh worktree off **origin/main** (never the stale local main; never `git rebase` the branch's 3 stray commits — they are superseded near-dups of 45c34d3d/95150a92 already on main). Re-apply the 15-file keep-list as uncommitted changes.
2. Move the wall chain into shared `AuthoringWall.enforce/5`, mounted at **both** lifecycle.ex and block_ops.ex `upsert_paper`.
3. **ABSORB, don't reinvent:** origin/main's lifecycle.ex now has +99/-17 of #2817 inline (D28 ratchet + telemetry). The worktree's lifecycle.ex diff was built against the simpler pre-#2817 file, so it **will NOT drop in cleanly** (the "byte-identical / zero-drift / clean drop-in" survey claim was true only vs *stale local* main). The builder must carry origin/main's `emit_wall_rejection` telemetry **into** the shared module, or `lifecycle_test.exs:486-507` goes red once the wall moves out of lifecycle.ex.
4. **PRESERVE #2818's error heads** and **KEEP the worktree's D26 tags/description passthrough** (still missing on origin/main — the only genuinely-net-new ingest work). These live in different regions of the ingest controller and should merge, but that must be PROVEN.
5. The 4-caller audit is settled: exactly **4** lib callers (seeds/clean, plan_papers, 2 ingest heads), not 13; the worktree resolves all 4. The "13" was a miscount.
6. The **~288-fixture / 117-callsite / 40-file mechanical sweep is 0% started** — only the `LabelFixtures.paper_attrs/2` wrapper exists. This is the bulk of remaining volume and the prime DECOMPOSE candidate (Fable exhausted → both halves are opus; split the mechanical sweep from the delicate reconciliation).

## Ledger corrections Decide must make
- `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry` — **leave CLOSED**; annotate that it landed via #2817 and the extraction absorbs it into the shared module. Do not reopen.
- `ae-ingest-honest-errors` (D27 heads) — **already landed inline via #2818**; do not file/build as new. Only the D26 passthrough remains, folded into the primary. (Note: those #2818 heads are effectively dead code until the wall is mounted at upsert_paper — the extraction activates them.)
- `ae-caller-error-surfacing` (#2793) — verify-only, done; mark CLOSED to stop it re-propagating as a phantom carry.

## Coverage map

**Checked and FOUND (load-bearing, high-confidence):**
- origin/main carries #2817 (D28+telemetry), #2818 (D27 heads), #2793 (caller-error-surfacing) — Digest git-proven, not read-proven.
- Worktree fork = 99eb9583, 25 behind origin/main; fork predates #2817/#2818.
- Worktree `authoring_wall.ex` (215 lines): enforce/5 chain, exemption-read-once, clear-after-full-pass, recompute-else-drop, raw-tuple return, self-id via ref.doc_id → DedupWall — all present and correct; **telemetry absent**.
- All 3 `upsert_paper` delegations thread `opts \\ []` in the worktree; main is single-arity.
- Exactly 4 real lib callers; worktree resolves all 4 (2 bypass_wall+rationale, 2 ingest enforce+passthrough).
- Mechanical-sweep scope exact: 41 files / 117 callsites, minus ingest-controller-test (3) = **40 files / 114 callsites**, 0% swept.
- Gate mechanics: worktree has self-contained deps + _build/test; `CC=clang mix test` runs green on the wall/lifecycle/ingest files (34 tests) — but at the STALE pre-rebase state.
- upsert_paper is the last unwalled published-paper/task path; task claim/close/move (D6) only touch content/rev, never status/tags/main_tag — a correctly-scoped exemption.
- editor write-loss bug real: `paper_field_block.ex:614-615` `ensure_map` catch-all discards a legacy flat-string tag row on edit; read side renders blank via `composite_field.ex:391`.

**Checked and NOT found (absences = decisions-in-waiting):**
- **Telemetry in the worktree extraction** — the shared module has none; the primary MUST carry origin/main's inline telemetry across the extraction seam (net *move*, not net *invent*).
- **D26 tags/description passthrough on origin/main ingest** — absent; only the worktree WIP has it. Without it a "compliant" ingest POST still can't register tags.
- **The mechanical sweep applied** — wrapper built, 0 of 40 files swept.
- **A dedicated `block_ops.ex` upsert_paper test** — none exists; "miss one delegation and the bypass silently dies" has no protective test.
- **Ingest advisory (soft-dup 0.30–0.55 band) delivery** — `Warnings.reset/drain` is called only by mutate_controller + studio_live/shared, NOT the ingest controller; advise-band warnings are queued into a never-reset process-dict and dropped. Decide must rule: wire it (reset/drain + a `warnings` envelope key) or explicitly defer to v2.
- **The composite subfield key for the write-loss fix** — surveyor could not confirm `%{"tag"=>s}` is the real weighted-tags subfield name against the schema; unverified.

**Corners no surveyor reached:**
- `content/edges.ex`, `content/sheets.ex`, onixedit `staleness_live.ex` / `bokbasen/status.ex` — surfaced by grep as `Document.changeset` callers, never individually read (domain names imply non-walled types; not proven clean).
- The full Elixir suite post-rebase — only the wall-adjacent files were run, and only at the stale pre-rebase HEAD.
- `bp search` — no surveyor could run it (no such verb in this CLI build); no prior-art query against Barkpark's own papers/tasks succeeded. Ledger truth was established via git + `bp task get`.

## Contradictions resolved
- **"main byte-identical / clean drop-in" (main-lifecycle-wall-anchors) vs "D28 fully landed on origin/main" (d28-fate-and-ledger)** → the latter is correct; the former read stale local main. The reconciliation is NON-trivial (lifecycle.ex drifted +99/-17 via #2817).
- **"telemetry absent from main, build it net-new" (exemption-telemetry-sites) vs origin/main reality** → telemetry EXISTS inline on origin/main; the work is to MOVE it into the shared module, same event name/shape, and re-green the existing test.
- **"contamination reverts chat-tui/hyperquiz/listen" (2 surveyors) vs "git status shows only 15 wall files" (main-lifecycle-wall-anchors)** → both true; the reversions live only in the stale-branch DIFF, not in uncommitted edits. Building FRESH off origin/main and re-applying the 15-file keep-list sidesteps it entirely.

---

## Verify fleet (in flight — 5 assignments)

| # | model | question | proof RUN |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | opus | Does re-applying the 15-file keep-list onto CURRENT origin/main compile, and does moving the wall out of lifecycle.ex break the #2817 telemetry test (proving telemetry must be carried into AuthoringWall)? Does the ingest controller end up with BOTH #2818 error heads AND the worktree's tags/description passthrough? | fresh worktree off origin/main, cp keep-list, `CC=clang mix compile`, `mix test lifecycle_test.exs authoring_wall_mount_test.exs bulldocs_ingest_wall_test.exs` — red/green observed, not read |
| V2 | sonnet | Confirm origin/main ancestry of #2817/#2818/#2793 and the live ledger state of ae-upsert-paper-wall / ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry / ae-ingest-honest-errors; confirm the 3 stray branch commits are superseded dups (do-not-replay). | `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, `git log --grep`, `bp task get` |
| V3 | opus | Is the write-loss bug live on origin/main, and what is the REAL composite subfield key the one-line `ensure_map` fix must reconstitute into (`tag` vs other)? Wrong key = silent corruption persists. | read origin/main `paper_field_block.ex` + the weighted-tags composite schema definition; write+run a targeted `ensure_map` unit test if feasible |
| V4 | sonnet | Prove the mechanical sweep is REAL, not vacuous: with enforcement on-by-default, do a sample of the 40 fixture-bearing test files actually go RED without the LabelFixtures.paper_attrs wrapper? Confirm 40-files/114-callsites count. | in V1's probe worktree, run 3-4 sample fixture test files → observe failures; `grep -c` the callsite count |
| V5 | sonnet | Re-anchor the last-bypass completeness to origin/main and read the 4 unread `Document.changeset` sites (edges/sheets/onixedit x2); confirm the ingest advisory dead-letter (no Warnings.reset/drain in the ingest controller) on origin/main so Decide can rule wire-vs-defer. | `git grep` origin/main for Document.changeset callers + Warnings.reset/drain; read the 4 sites |

*Status: VERIFYING. Next: Decide folds verifier proofs, corrects the ledger (no reopen of ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry; D27 already landed), rules on decompose + advisory, and cuts the wave plan before builders fly.*

---

# DECIDE — verifier proofs folded, ledger corrected, wave cut (2026-07-13)

## What verification proved (trust the run output)

**The whole wave pivots on one correction, now triple-proven: the survey baselines were read against a STALE LOCAL main.** Local `main` (16e259ee) trailed `origin/main` (7e037ca1) by ~19+ commits. Everything the strategy brief called "false-done" was that artifact.

- **#2817 / #2818 / #2793 are ALL ancestors of origin/main** (V1, V2, V4 independently). V2's proof: `for c in d343c793 f1fc2832 900981af; do git merge-base --is-ancestor $c origin/main; done → d343c793 ON / f1fc2832 ON / 900981af ON`. So D28 ratchet+telemetry, D27 honest-ingest heads, and D23 caller-surfacing are **already on main**. `ae-w4-ratchet-telemetry`, `ae-ingest-honest-errors`, `ae-caller-error-surfacing` stay DONE — reopening any is itself a false claim.
- **A naive cp of the worktree WIP REVERTS #2817's telemetry** (V1, run end-to-end). Proof: after wholesale keep-list applied, `lifecycle_test.exs:486 ... Assertion failed, no matching message after 100ms. The process mailbox is empty ... 36 tests, 1 failure` — the `[:barkpark,:authoring,:wall_rejection]` event never fired because the worktree's `authoring_wall.ex` has D28 recompute-else-drop but ZERO telemetry. Adding a ~20-line else-seam that emits `emit_wall_rejection` re-GREENs it: `24 tests, 0 failures`.
- **#2818 heads + D26 passthrough co-exist green** (V1): restored origin/main's controller (render_error heads at :131-138/:187-194) + re-added the 8-line tags/description passthrough into both attrs whitelists → `21 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped`.
- **The mount reds 16 pre-existing ingest fixtures, one shape** (V1): `29 tests, 16 failures ... {:label_spine, %{field: "description", ...}}` — every failure a bare `{:ok,_} = upsert_paper` bind. **The sweep is real and separable.**
- **The sweep is 40 files / 114 callsites and mechanical** (V4): raw grep `43 files / 134 callsites` minus the WIP's own `authoring_wall_mount_test.exs` (16), `label_fixtures.ex`'s doc-comment hit (1), and `bulldocs_ingest_controller_test.exs` (3, core-owned) = 40/114. Wrapping hollow_test.exs's 3 callsites in `LabelFixtures.paper_attrs/1` took it `8 failures → 0 failures` with no other change.
- **The editor write-loss key is "tag"** (V3), double-proven: schema `paper.json:22 {"name":"tag",...}` AND validator `label_spine.ex main_tag → get(top,"tag")`. Bug live at `paper_field_block.ex:614-615`. The surveyor's second citation `composite_field.ex` is STALE — `git show origin/main:...composite_field.ex → fatal: path does not exist`. Genericity caveat pinned: `ensure_map` is generic across all arrayOf composites.
- **upsert_paper is genuinely the LAST bypass** (V5 + last-bypass survey): the 4 grep-flagged `Document.changeset` sites (edges.ex/sheets.ex/onixedit staleness_live.ex + bokbasen/status.ex) never write status/tags/main_tag on a walled type (`@walled_types ~w(paper task)`). Advisory dead-letter confirmed real but fails safe (`Warnings` collect-only-when-listening; ingest controller has no reset/drain).

**Coverage / not-founds worth carrying:** the preserved worktree is ~22-25 behind origin/main (NOT 100 — that was local main); its 6 "contamination" files show EMPTY diff (refuted); its 3 commits are already ancestors of origin/main (replay = no-op). Full post-rebase Elixir suite NOT run by any verifier (the primary builder owns that). No bp-search prior-art query succeeded (CLI has no task-search verb reachable that way).

## Decisions (D33–D38 — mirror the charter)

- **D33** — False-done REFUTED (stale-local-main artifact). #2817/#2818/#2793 all on origin/main → reopen NOTHING. The 4 Document.changeset sites are not bypasses; upsert_paper is the last.
- **D34** — Primary is a 3-way RECONCILIATION, not a cp: re-apply keep-list, CARRY telemetry across the seam, PRESERVE #2818 heads, keep D26 passthrough, delete the 3 D27 skips + upgrade the ingest_wall assertion.
- **D35** — DECOMPOSE core extraction from the 40-file/114-callsite sweep (Fable exhausted, both opus); sweep sequences after the core on its branch, file sets disjoint.
- **D36** — Ingest advisory dead-letter DEFERRED to backlog (fails safe; a public-envelope shape change; collides on the ingest controller with the primary).
- **D37** — `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` PROMOTED; key "tag" double-proven; ship with a non-tag-composite round-trip protective test.
- **D38** — 3 opus slices, finish-weighted; verify-only residue = #2793 caller-surfacing.

## Wave plan (in flight — 3 opus slices)

| Slice | task_id | surface | model | size | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core reconciliation (RESUME worktree) | `ae-upsert-paper-wall` | Elixir content/lifecycle + ingest | opus | large | `cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark/content/lifecycle_test.exs test/barkpark/content/papers/authoring_wall_mount_test.exs test/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_ingest_wall_test.exs test/barkpark_web/controllers/bulldocs_ingest_controller_test.exs` |
| Fixture sweep (40 files/114 callsites) | `ae-fixture-sweep` | Elixir test fixtures | opus | medium | `cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test` on the 40 swept files (branch from the core; mount must be present) |
| Editor legacy-tag write-loss | `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss` | Studio LiveView (paper_field_block.ex) | opus | small | `cd api && CC=clang MIX_ENV=test mix test <new paper_editor test>` |

Backlog filed this wave: `ae-ingest-advisory-deadletter` (D36). Still open: `ae-curator-feed`, `ae-dedup-trgm-index`, `ae-paper-decision-sync`.

*Status: BUILDING. The core is a RESUME — the builder continues the preserved worktree's WIP reconciled onto origin/main, does not restart. Review closes this story.*


---

# REVIEW — the last bypass sealed (wave 4 complete, 2026-07-13)

*Reviewer (Fable), last hands before merge. Reviewed all 3 green slices end-to-end, fixed one cross-slice break in place, re-ran every gate on the true integrated tree. **Grade: A-.***

## What shipped (per slice, integration-ordered core → sweep → editor)

**S1 — `ae-upsert-paper-wall` (core).** Final branch `loop-epic/seal-the-last-wall-bypass-authoringwall--0-r`. `Barkpark.Content.AuthoringWall.enforce/5` is now the ONE shared chain: exemption-read-once → label spine → E3 registry → E4 dedup → clear-on-FULL-pass → main_tag stamp. `Lifecycle.publish_document` delegates byte-identically (its 225-line inline chain is gone). `BlockOps.upsert_paper` mounts the same chain on a synthesized `%Document{}` ref (doc_id = slug) BEFORE the Repo write — the self-id reaches DedupWall's incumbent exclusion so a paper can never near-duplicate itself. D34 reconciliation verified clean: telemetry CARRIED into `enforce`'s else-seam (the `[:barkpark,:authoring,:wall_rejection]` event + `Logger.warning` fire live in the gate run for all three codes), #2818 render_error heads preserved, D26 tags/description passthrough added to both ingest attrs whitelists, the 3 D27 skips activated, the ingest_wall tagless assertion upgraded to `code=label_spine`. `opts \\ []` threaded through ALL three delegations (content.ex / papers.ex / block_ops.ex). Caller audit complete: 2 ingest heads ENFORCE, plan_papers + seeds/clean + 4 priv seeds carry `bypass_wall: true` + a grep-able rationale. **Gate 65/0.** The mount test is genuinely non-vacuous — verified `write_encrypted_paper` seeds `base_content` from the existing row, so the recompute-else-drop test's stale `main_tag` is really present and really dropped. One deliberate improvement over the pre-extraction behavior: `stamp_main_tag/2` scopes recompute-else-drop to `@walled_types`, so a non-walled type now keeps a user field named `main_tag` instead of having it silently eaten.

**S2 — `ae-fixture-sweep`.** Final branch `loop-epic/fixture-sweep-wrap-40-test-files-114-ups-1-r` (= core + sweep, stacked). 114 callsites across 40 files wrapped in `LabelFixtures.paper_attrs/1`; 2 callsites needed semantic hand-edits (content_projection_test, sharing_composition_p4_test's ingest POST). **Stacked gate 499/0 across all 40 files.** Completeness PROVEN, not asserted: the set-difference of {every test file referencing `upsert_paper`} minus {files touched by any slice} is EMPTY (44 files, all covered). The single ingest-referencing file not touched (`capabilities_project_test`) is a capability-tier visibility test, not a paper birth. No uncovered wall-facing path remains.

**S3 — `ae-editor-legacy-tag-writeloss`.** Final branch `loop-epic/paperfieldblock-composite-editor-must-no-2-r` (= core + editor + reviewer fix). Two seams: a RENDER seam (`normalize_legacy_composite_rows`, SCOPED to composites that declare a `"tag"` subfield) reconstitutes a legacy bare-string row to `%{"tag"=>s}` before the editor renders it; plus the charter-mandated generic `ensure_map` `is_binary` merge head as belt-and-suspenders. The protective test reds without the fix and greens with it; two genericity-guard tests pin a non-tag composite (amount/currency) and a scalar arrayOf (keywords) round-tripping unharmed with NO spurious `tag` key. **Directory gate 103/0 on the integration.**

## What the reviewer fixed in place (the one real blemish)

The editor slice was filed "independent, parallel-safe" — it is NOT. Its seed helpers, and the shared `PaperEditorTestHelpers` it `use`s (which the sweep wrapped), birth papers through bare `upsert_paper` with no tags. The merged wall 422s those births. The slice's declared gate (`mix test .../paper_editor/`) passed ONLY because it ran on the editor's own branch WITHOUT the wall present — a textbook vacuous green (the right thing did not produce the pass). Re-run on the true integrated tree, the editor test reds 3/3 with `{:label_spine, field: "description"}`. **Reviewer fix:** `bypass_wall: true` on the 3 seed helpers (editor-mechanics fixtures, wall not under test, bypass keeps the seeded blocks pristine for the exact-HTML render + round-trip assertions). Committed on the editor -r branch; integrated gate now 103/0.

## Cross-slice reality the lead MUST honor

These are ONE integrated unit, not three independent merges. Because D35 split the mount (breaks ~288 fixtures) from the sweep (repairs them), **a core-only PR REDS the full Elixir Test gate.** Merge order MUST be core → sweep → editor, stacked. All three -r branches carry the single core commit (git dedupes on merge); the slice file sets are disjoint; the full gate is green only on the combined tip. The editor slice depends on BOTH core (for `bypass_wall/2` to compile) AND sweep (for the shared helper wrap). Confidence net beyond the slice gates: content+papers dirs 829/0; web-controllers+studio 2154/1, where the 1 is the documented studio-chat async sandbox-ownership flake (`chat_live_test` passes 274/0 in isolation, unrelated to the wall).

## Ledger audit

Honest across all three tasks: each `in_progress`, every built criterion stamped `met` with evidence as the work happened, the merge-gated criterion left `met=false` for the lead to close on merge. No lies or omissions to correct. The reviewer's editor-seed fix is recorded here and in the charter wave log, not as a criterion flip.

## Grade: A-

The wave FINISHES the epic's central promise — one fail-closed door for every published paper and task, the last bypass sealed — with high correctness and PROVEN completeness (the sweep's coverage is a set-difference, not a claim), and it REDUCES duplication (a shared chokepoint replaces two forked chains). The single deduction is the editor slice's vacuous green: its gate passed pre-integration and would have reddened the merge, requiring reviewer intervention to catch — exactly the distrust-vacuous-green lesson the charter carries. The delivered, fixed, integrated result is excellent.

*Status: COMPLETE. The wall is mounted at all FIVE seams. Remaining epic work is backlog observability + doc-truth (see the charter wave log), none blocking the north star.*
