# PortableDoc Everything-Editable — Reconcile-and-Close Wave of 2026-07-11 **Epic anchor:** `pd-everything-editable` — "EPIC · PortableDoc Beta: everything editable, 1:1 with the reader (finish line)" (priority 1, open). **Wave status: COMPLETE** — reviewed, graded A-, debrief at the bottom. (Earlier statuses: SURVEYING → DECIDING → BUILDING; this line is the living status field.) This Paper is the wave's story end to end: direction → survey → verification → decisions → build → debrief. ## The wish Verify the anchor's own criteria against HEAD and either close honestly or finish honestly: - **(a)** if "everything editable, 1:1 with the reader" is fully evidenced (91-block showcase verified view+edit+TUI; view-edit-parity harness exists — run one if cheap), stamp each criterion with file:line + PR evidence and **CLOSE the epic**; - **(b)** if the anchor names genuinely unbuilt finish-line work, cut the **smallest honest wave**. Do not invent scope; do not relitigate shipped doctrine. Hard constraints: render-path unification law (never fork reader/editor paths); .ex/.heex waits for Elixir Test; goldens byte-unchanged except owned regens; hollow-paper gate is live on every write seam; worktrees from origin/main after git fetch; builders claim first; PR body carries `Task: `. File under `pd-everything-editable`. ## What the strategist found in five minutes 1. **The ledger is 9/10 done but the anchor is unstamped.** All 3 acceptance criteria sit `met: false` with EMPTY evidence. The only open child is `pd-ee-live-verify` — "HUMAN GATE · Live Studio pass: nested-editing UX for table/columns/section/figure/terminal". 2. **The catch-all is alive.** Criterion 1 anchors on `paper_editor.ex:1312`; at HEAD it lives at `api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live/components/paper_editor.ex:1339` — "<%= @type %> blocks are not editable yet (view/delete/reorder only)". Whether any authorable type can still REACH it is unknown and is the wave's central factual question. 3. **The editable surface grew AFTER the initiative was recorded complete.** Memory records everything-editable COMPLETE 2026-07-07; composition-doctrine wave 2 (#2398) merged /card authoring + full card slot editing 2026-07-10. The 36-type parity matrix predates card, quiz, tickets, and any other new block types — the matrix and the "everything" claim both need re-baselining against HEAD's compose.ex registry. 4. **The three criteria have three different verification shapes:** C1 is a mechanical enumeration (registry × editor coverage); C2 is a gate run (parity gate green + view-edit-parity harness); C3 is a LIVE browser pass currently labeled a human gate — the one child that has never been satisfied. ## Strategic direction (tentative — Decide finalizes) **This is a reconcile-and-close wave with at most a sliver of build.** The finished experience: the anchor either closed with all 3 criteria stamped (file:line + PR + gate-run evidence), or open carrying exactly the honest remainder — a named list of block types that still hit the catch-all, nothing else. Four streams, lean order: 1. **Evidence C1 mechanically.** Enumerate the authorable block registry at HEAD (compose.ex ground truth) against paper_editor coverage; list every type that reaches the 1339 catch-all. Empty list → stamp. Non-empty → those exact types are the wave's only build scope. 2. **Evidence C2 by running the gates.** Parity gate on HEAD + a fresh view-edit-parity harness run over the current block set (including card slots). Green → stamp with the run as evidence. 3. **Resolve C3 / pd-ee-live-verify.** Leaning: execute the live pass ourselves via chrome-devtools against a running Studio (local host = admin, no auth gate; fall back to guerrilla if local boot blockers bite), driving nested editing for table/columns/section/figure/terminal on the 91-block showcase, screenshots as evidence. If the gate's wording truly mandates a human, package a ready-to-run checklist + leave ONLY that child open while stamping what's stampable. 4. **Name the successor, don't absorb it.** Render-path unification is the recorded endgame but is NOT one of this anchor's criteria — verify that reading is right, record unification as a separate successor epic/task, and refuse scope creep into it. Also owed: an evidence audit of the 9 done children (false-done fabrication happened in this repo 2026-07-08 — distrust vacuous done). ## Survey plan (16 surveyors, in flight) | # | Key | Question | Why it changes the plan | |---|-----|----------|------------------------| | 1 | block-registry-vs-editor | Every authorable type in compose.ex vs editor coverage; which types reach paper_editor.ex:1339 at HEAD | This IS criterion 1; empty list = close, non-empty = the whole build scope | | 2 | card-wave2-surface | What #2398 shipped (/card authoring, card slot editing); is card fully editable | Newest surface growth; most likely C1 gap | | 3 | new-blocks-since-matrix | Block types added after 2026-07-07 (quiz, tickets, canvas, storm…) + their editor/reader coverage | The 36-type matrix is stale; re-baseline "everything" | | 4 | parity-gate-state | Locate the parity gate; is it green on HEAD; what byte-alignment it actually proves | Criterion 2 evidence source | | 5 | view-edit-parity-harness | The view-edit-parity skill: cost, last report, would a fresh run evidence C2 | Cheap-run decision for Digest | | 6 | live-verify-brief | Full brief of pd-ee-live-verify: exact wording; agent-driven browser pass allowed or human-mandated | Decides the C3 path (drive it vs package it) | | 7 | studio-boot-recipe | Working recipe for a live Studio (local boot blockers vs guerrilla); how to load the showcase | Feasibility of the browser pass this wave | | 8 | showcase-evidence | 91-block showcase + #1592: exactly what was verified view+edit+TUI | May already part-evidence C2/C3 | | 9 | done-children-audit | Do the 9 done children's claims hold at HEAD (section title-persistence, fleet edit islands, insertability)? | False-done risk; close must not stand on fabricated evidence | | 10 | render-path-unification-scope | Reader vs editor render path state; is unification tracked anywhere; confirm it is NOT an anchor criterion | Successor-naming vs scope creep | | 11 | fleet-blocks-status | pd-ee-fleet-editors reality; which fleet/task-* islands stay read-only per the human decision, and does that trip C1 | The decided read-only set must be subtracted from "everything" | | 12 | hollow-paper-gate-interplay | Does the hollow-paper gate constrain editor writes / a live insert pass | Avoid a browser pass that fails by construction | | 13 | prior-papers-tasks | bp search query sweep: prior everything-editable / parity / showcase papers+tasks; what past waves left as remaining | Don't re-decide decided things | | 14 | editor-test-coverage | Test files covering paper_editor/paper_canvas editing; flakes; what Elixir Test would gate | Build-slice cost estimate | | 15 | tui-parity-stance | Does "1:1 with the reader" include TUI pdrender per the anchor/children wording; new-block TUI coverage | Scope boundary of the 1:1 claim | | 16 | slash-menu-insertability | Are the newest blocks (card etc.) insertable from the slash menu (pd-ee-insertability drift check) | Editable-but-uninsertable would be a hollow close | ## Ledger links - Epic anchor: task `pd-everything-editable` (this Paper's id stamped on its `wave_paper`; `wave_status` = surveying). - Open child: `pd-ee-live-verify`. Slice tasks: filed at Decide; each will carry this Paper's id. --- *Appended by later phases: Survey digest + verify plan (Digest) → decisions + wave plan (Decide) → debrief (Review).* --- ## Survey digest (Digest phase, 2026-07-11) **Wave status: VERIFYING** — 16 surveys in, digest folded, 6-verifier fleet in flight. ### Established (file:line-anchored; trust these) 1. **C1 is FALSE at HEAD — but the gap is exactly 5 type-strings.** Fresh registry×editor enumeration: `stat`, `stats`, `stat-grid`, `heatmap`, `chart` (registered in `compose.ex:1115-1145`, backed by `Render.DataViz`) have ZERO editor coverage — absent from `@canvas_types` (paper_canvas.ex), from paper_editor.ex's case clauses, and from all fleet/figure lists — so they fall to the not-editable-yet catch-all, now at `paper_editor.ex:1339` (the anchor's `:1312` citation is stale). Everything else in the ~48-type registry is covered (42 canvas-eligible types + explicit case clauses for image and composite/arrayOf/codelist/localizedText). The 5 DataViz types are NOT slash-insertable (CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES = exactly 23, lockstep-tested and green on HEAD) — they reach the catch-all only via API-authored content opened in Studio. 2. **The epic's own text is stale twice over**: the "REMAINING: section/figure/action/terminal…" list is done (all canvas-eligible at HEAD), and the catch-all line number moved. The linked 36-type parity-matrix artifact is UNFETCHABLE (deleted/unshared) — the fresh enumeration supersedes it. 3. **#2398 (composition wave 2) closed a gap, didn't open one.** `card` became insertable + fully slot-editable (title/body/media/action, slots.ex:115-121) atomically in commit 5dd34bbd; JS smoke suite (26 files incl. __cards.test.mjs) green on HEAD. No new quiz/tickets/canvas/storm block types exist — that premise is dead. 4. **The 9 done children hold at HEAD.** 4 properly evidenced (PRs #1235, #1568 confirmed merged); 5 are "vacuous ledger" (met:0, evidence:'') but code-verified TRUE (PR #1233 ancestor of HEAD; __section_parity.test.mjs ran 11/11 PASS live). Bookkeeping defect, not fabrication — they need retroactive evidence stamps, not rework. 5. **C2's gate = two Elixir test files riding blocking `mix test`** (view_edit_parity_test.exs: prose CSS byte-parity; canvas_reader_parity_gate_test.exs: fleet one-producer + mutation-proven teeth). Green on 5dd34bbd (CI run 29128511425: 9941 tests, 0 failures); the run on current HEAD was still pending at survey time. **Neither file covers the singular `card`** — card parity rides component_golden_parity_test.exs + shared-class construction instead. 6. **Do NOT re-run view-edit-parity.workflow.js as-is**: ~450+ agent calls, and its RENDER_EX constant now points at a defdelegate facade (logic moved to compose.ex/walk.ex) with a stale inline-style premise. The 2026-07-05 parity matrix report predates #2398 and never mentions card. 7. **C3 is agent-drivable.** pd-ee-live-verify's "HUMAN GATE" label documents a session-specific Chrome-profile-lock blocker, not a human mandate (contrast: pd-ee-fleet-config-decision, a real user-judgment gate). A local Studio is ALREADY RUNNING at localhost:4000 (admin, no login gate; showcase paper live at /papers/portabledoc-showcase, 135KB). **What keeps it off A/A+:** the mounted card node-view and the DataViz islands are proven by construction + source-pinned tests, not by a live browser — real, accepted risk (C3 is infra-blocked, charter D9), but a runtime paint bug would still only surface at pd-ee-live-verify. S2/S3 built the shared bundle from different bases, leaving the predicted collision to be reconciled by hand in review — the stack is clean now, but the wave design pushed that integration risk to the last phase. And the v1 JSON islands for heatmap/chart are honest but austere UX (deferred to pd-ee-dataviz-structured-editors by decision, so noted, not double-counted).

## Next wave

The anchor's close ceremony is now gated ONLY on C3. Priorities: (1) unblock `pd-ee-chrome-mcp-userdatadir` (per-session userDataDir) then execute `pd-ee-live-verify`'s 7-step checklist — now including a card-slot pass and a DataViz island round-trip; (2) with C1+C2 evidence stamped at merge and C3 evidenced live, run the close ceremony on `pd-everything-editable`. Do NOT pull the p3 backlog (structured DataViz editors, sheet/embed audit, reader stale-cache) into the close path.</article>

Each PR body carries its `Task: `. - On merge, close the merge-gated criterion ("PR merged") on each of the three tasks, AND close `pd-ee-root-heex-card-comment` (its fix rides S2-r, evidence already stamped). - When S3 merges, **C1 flips genuinely TRUE**: stamp the anchor's first criterion with the S3 PR + `paper_canvas.ex @canvas_dataviz_types` evidence. Reviewer mutations: review_note stamped on all three slice tasks (final branch names + merge order), and `pd-ee-root-heex-card-comment` moved to in_progress with met:true evidence (fix rides S2-r; lead closes on merge). No ledger lies found; no out-of-wave tasks touched. ## Grade: A- (earned, not asserted) **Genuinely strong:** every slice is exactly its brief with zero scope creep; the render-path-unification law held everywhere (S3 paints through `Render.render_block/2`, S2 emits the reader's own shape rather than reviving a mirror); the test additions are load-bearing, not decorative (`__card_parity` pins the mounted shape AND the forbidden literal; `__dataviz` exercises the exact island logic the browser runs; parity-gate fixtures carry real data so no vacuous empty-box green); builder self-reviews were honest about blind spots, and chasing them found nothing false. reader_contract.text:
Onboarding-composition — Wave 2 strategy
Epic: onboarding-composition-epic · Wave: 2 · Phase: SURVEYING · Model: Opus-only (Fable exhausted) · Opened: 2026-07-14
This Paper is the wave's living story. Strategize opened it; Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends decisions + the wave plan + the fresh charter; Review closes it as the debrief. Fan-out workers never write here — they write their own bp task; the next Fable folds their reports in.
The wish (verbatim intent)
Wave 1 landed grade A- (paper bp-onboarding-composition-wave-2026-07-13): the ONE-transaction ONE-receipt onboarding — nothing → authenticated → MCP-connected → correct-team instance → a proven read-only tool call, under 5 min, never printing the bearer. Wave 2 ships the identity-composition slices already filed and ready:
BP-ONB-02/03 — Team-aware CLI identity: bp teams / bp team use + --team instance credentials, so a user selects and pins the right team's instance.
BP-ONB-04 — Provision with BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL: so the Cloud-to-Studio login button actually renders.
BP-ONB-05/12 — Instance-ID identity: URL aliases + BOM-tolerant config parsing + a whoami receipt (instance ID, team, URL+aliases, auth tier, MCP tool-catalog version+names, read-only call result, exact client-reload instruction).
Ground every slice in the wave-1 paper and the epic's filed child tasks. Each slice needs a behavioral proof — a real first-time flow, Windows/BOM path included.
Strategic direction
The finished experience: a first-time Windows user, coming from Barkpark Cloud, runs bp once and the CLI knows who they are, which team they belong to, and which instance is that team's — with no phantom "-2" duplicate servers, no config bricked by a Notepad BOM, and a single bp whoami / doctor receipt that reads back the whole identity in one honest envelope. From the Cloud side, provisioning stamps BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL so Studio renders the "sign in via Cloud" button instead of a dead corner. Identity becomes composed and legible end-to-end, not scattered across URL-string keys.
The load-bearing reconciliation (surveyors must nail this first): the epic task's wave_status claims wave 1 built "8/8 slices" — but the local checkout / origin main shows internal/cli/config.go with no InstanceID, no Aliases, and no BOM strip; the ServerEntry is still keyed purely by normalized URL. This matches the KNOWN failure mode of wave 1 (Decide committed to a diverged LOCAL main and never PR'd — same reason the wave-1 charter is stranded on neither origin nor local). So wave 2 likely builds the identity PLUMBING fresh, not merely activates it. Every builder must diff its target files against origin/main before writing, and treat wave-1 "done" claims as unverified until proven.
Choices I lean toward (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds):
Key identity by InstanceID first, URL second. Add InstanceID string + Aliases []string to ServerEntry; key Remember/Find/IsActive/DisplayName by InstanceID when known, fall back to normalized-URL only for ID-less bare local dev. A second hostname of a known instance folds into Aliases, never mints a "-2". Source of truth for the ID: the control plane's DomainStatusResult.Instance.ID + Domains[] (already modeled in internal/cloudclient/client.go).
Wire the ID at connect/attach (task-e6b0bc97130bae89) — plumbing is inert until a caller stamps the real ID. This is the E2E activation: one instance via two hostnames → one ServerEntry.
BOM tolerance is a one-line strip (bytes.TrimPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF,0xBB,0xBF})) before Unmarshal in LoadConfig; SaveConfig already emits BOM-free JSON and self-heals. Prove it with a failing-first test (TestBOMBricksLoadConfig flips to green).
whoami is the receipt spine. Extend bp whoami -o json (builtins.go) to carry instance_id + aliases[] + team + auth_tier + MCP catalog version/names + read-only call result + the exact client-reload instruction. The onboarding doctor composes over this — don't fork a second receipt.

The finished experience: a first-time Windows user, coming from Barkpark Cloud, runs bp once and the CLI knows who they are, which team they belong to, and which instance is that team's — with no phantom "-2" duplicate servers, no config bricked by a Notepad BOM, and a single bp whoami / doctor receipt that reads back the whole identity in one honest envelope. From the Cloud side, provisioning stamps BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL so Studio renders the "sign in via Cloud" button instead of a dead corner. Identity becomes composed and legible end-to-end, not scattered across URL-string keys.

The load-bearing reconciliation (surveyors must nail this first): the epic task's wave_status claims wave 1 built "8/8 slices" — but the local checkout / origin main shows internal/cli/config.go with no InstanceID, no Aliases, and no BOM strip; the ServerEntry is still keyed purely by normalized URL. This matches the KNOWN failure mode of wave 1 (Decide committed to a diverged LOCAL main and never PR'd — same reason the wave-1 charter is stranded on neither origin nor local). So wave 2 likely builds the identity PLUMBING fresh, not merely activates it. Every builder must diff its target files against origin/main before writing, and treat wave-1 "done" claims as unverified until proven.

Choices I lean toward (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds):

  • Key identity by InstanceID first, URL second. Add InstanceID string + Aliases []string to ServerEntry; key Remember/Find/IsActive/DisplayName by InstanceID when known, fall back to normalized-URL only for ID-less bare local dev. A second hostname of a known instance folds into Aliases, never mints a "-2". Source of truth for the ID: the control plane's DomainStatusResult.Instance.ID + Domains[] (already modeled in internal/cloudclient/client.go).
  • Wire the ID at connect/attach (task-e6b0bc97130bae89) — plumbing is inert until a caller stamps the real ID. This is the E2E activation: one instance via two hostnames → one ServerEntry.
  • BOM tolerance is a one-line strip (bytes.TrimPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF,0xBB,0xBF})) before Unmarshal in LoadConfig; SaveConfig already emits BOM-free JSON and self-heals. Prove it with a failing-first test (TestBOMBricksLoadConfig flips to green).
  • whoami is the receipt spine. Extend bp whoami -o json (builtins.go) to carry instance_id + aliases[] + team + auth_tier + MCP catalog version/names + read-only call result + the exact client-reload instruction. The onboarding doctor composes over this — don't fork a second receipt.
  • Team model needs a real backend concept. bp teams / bp team use presuppose the server/control-plane models teams + memberships and can mint --team-scoped instance credentials. Whether that maps to existing tenancy/workspace scoping (bp cloud members, workspace-scoped tokens) is the biggest open design question — surveyors map it before Decide commits a shape.
  • BP-ONB-04 is a provisioning + Studio-render pair: stamp BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL at provision time (cloud/**) and make the Studio session view render the Cloud login button when it's present (session_controller.ex / session_html/new.html.heex). Backfill for existing instances is a separate backlog slice.

Prioritize: (1) origin-main truth reconciliation — everything downstream depends on whether we build or activate; (2) the ServerEntry identity core (BP-ONB-05/12) since 02/03/04 all read from it; (3) the team-model design question, because it's the one slice whose backend shape is genuinely uncertain.

Constraints held: Opus-only every phase (Fable exhausted, never Haiku). No charter file exists — reconstruct epic context from the epic task + wave-1 paper; Decide writes the charter FRESH and lands it via clean-extract (detached worktree off origin/main → copy charter → commit → PR → admin-merge), NEVER pushing diverged local main. Builders commit to LOCAL worktree branches and do NOT push; the steward pushes green branches. Keep every onboarding slice FILE-DISJOINT from the concurrent cloud-build W6 cycle (wf_fe674ef4-19d) running tenancy/search.

Survey plan (in flight now)

15 broad Sonnet surveyors cast a wide net. Each question + why it changes the plan:

  1. origin-main-truth — What identity code is ACTUALLY on origin/main? Diff config.go/servers_cmd.go/builtins.go for InstanceID/Aliases/BOM/team verbs; reconcile against the "8/8 done" wave_status. Why: decides build-fresh vs activate for every slice.
  2. serverentry-config-map — Full ServerEntry struct + RememberServer/FindServer/IsActiveServer/deriveUniqueName/DisplayName-collision + LoadConfig/SaveConfig + config.json schema. Why: 02/03/05/12 all mutate this one struct.
  3. control-plane-instance-shape — cloudclient DomainStatusResult.Instance{ID} + Domains[]; which fields are live at attach/connect; how bp attach/connect call the control plane. Why: the ID source for the whole identity fix.
  4. team-model-api — Does the server/control-plane model teams + memberships? Is there a /v1/teams route? What does a --team-scoped instance credential mean concretely? Why: BP-ONB-02/03 need a real backend team concept; this is the biggest unknown.
  5. tenancy-overlap — Existing tenancy/workspace scoping + bp cloud members + workspace-scoped tokens: does bp teams/team use overlap or extend it? Why: avoid building a parallel identity store; reuse the tenancy seam if it fits.
  6. whoami-receipt-current — Current bp whoami -o json fields (builtins.go), bp servers output, bp doctor. Why: the receipt must extend these, not fork.
  7. doctor-receipt-integration — onb-w1-onboarding-doctor-receipt: is the doctor built? How does it compose the receipt? Why: whoami feeds the doctor; the reload instruction + read-only call live here.
  8. mcp-catalog-in-receipt — Where's the MCP serve / tool catalog (bp-mcp-serve epic)? How does the receipt obtain catalog version + names + a read-only call result? Why: the receipt spec demands MCP fields.
  9. bom-config-parsing — LoadConfig Unmarshal path + existing config_test.go + Windows/Notepad save behavior. Why: BP-ONB-12 BOM tolerance + the failing-first test shape.
  10. barkpark-cloud-url-provision — Where instances are provisioned with env; where BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL is set/leaked today (base_url leak); provision path in cloud/**. Why: BP-ONB-04 stamps it at provision.
  11. studio-login-button — The Studio/session view that renders the Cloud login button (session_controller.ex, session_html/new.html.heex); what condition gates it (base_url vs cloud_url). Why: BP-ONB-04 makes it render.
  12. capabilities-base-url — How the capabilities endpoint emits base_url; onb-backlog-capabilities-base-url-alias; instance-ID + aliases in capabilities. Why: whoami/receipt + Studio button read this; possible backend slice.
  13. wave1-paper-decisions — Read the wave-1 paper fully: decisions D1-D34 (esp. D4 greenfield client-side identity, D27 identity, D34 workspace-slug resolve), what the charter must encode. Why: the fresh charter + all slices must honor prior decisions.
  14. concurrent-cycle-disjointness — What files does the cloud-build W6 cycle (wf_fe674ef4-19d, tenancy/search) touch right now? Open PRs + foreign claims. Why: onboarding slices must stay file-disjoint to avoid clobber.
  15. gate-and-build-mechanics — The Go gate (CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1); how internal/cli tests run; any Studio/api gate for BP-ONB-04; worktree isolation recipe. Why: builders need an exact, reproducible gate + isolation recipe.

Driven tasks

  • onboarding-composition-epic — epic anchor (carries wave_status + wave_paper)
  • onb-w1-team-aware-cli-identity — BP-ONB-02/03 (+BP-ONB-12 config half, whoami receipt)
  • onb-w1-instance-id-aliases-receipt — BP-ONB-05/12 plumbing
  • task-e6b0bc97130bae89 — BP-ONB-05 connect/attach ID-stamp activation (D4 wiring)
  • onb-backlog-cloud-url-fleet-backfill — BP-ONB-04 backfill BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL + fix base_url leak
  • onb-backlog-capabilities-base-url-alias — backend base_url from instance-ID + aliases

First job: reconcile the wave-1 diverged-local-main risk — origin/main config.go still lacks InstanceID/Aliases/BOM, so builders diff before building.

**Why.** The closing gate of the whole epic: a human-driven cross-surface visual audit that puts Studio, web, paper, and TUI side by side and confirms they read as one system — the qualitative complement to the automated drift gates.

**Approach.** Once the per-surface styleguides/sweeps land, capture each surface's styleguide + a representative real screen, review them together against the profile (colors, type, status vocab, lifecycle glyphs, motion), and file any residual drift as follow-ups. Record the audit + sign-off.

**Out of scope.** Fixing individual drifts (filed as follow-ups). This is the audit + sign-off gate.

Driven by spec §6 (drift) + §7 (sign-off) + the charter.

source.description:
Residual test coverage from the airdrop-grants close-out verification (2026-07-10). Both lanes were traced firsthand and HOLD today — this task adds the missing automated assertions so a regression is caught by a test, not a future audit. Not urgent; not a leak.

(a) SCOPED FEDERATED NARROWING: the /w/:ws scoped federated-search route (router.ex ~1665, pipe_through :scoped_api -> ResolveWorkspace) grant-narrows via resolve_workspace.ex:117-121 assigning grant_scoped_read -> scope_opts -> DocumentsRetriever base. This is proven ONLY by code-trace: federated_grant_deny_test.exs covers only the FLAT bare-:api route. Add a contract test mirroring federated_grant_deny_test for the scoped route: a grant-admitted non-member sees only grant-covered docs; an unowned token (positive control) sees everything; members byte-identical.

(b) REQUIRE-LOOPBACK 403 CONTRACT: /v1/data/local/search/:dataset (SearchController.search_local, pipeline :api_local) is safe solely because RequireLoopback (require_loopback.ex:20-34) halts non-127.0.0.0/8 / ::1 callers with a bodiless 403 — no test asserts this. A regression widening loopback?/1 would be caught by nothing. Add a plug/contract test: external remote_ip -> 403 halt; 127.0.0.1 and ::1 -> passes through.

Gate: CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test <the two new test files> — plus a deliberate-break check (invert the loopback guard locally, watch the new test go red) to prove non-vacuity.
source.title: Grant deny-matrix residual coverage — scoped-federated narrowing contract test + RequireLoopback 403 contract test

reader_contract.text:
Purpose
HIT LIVE while building site-spawner-w3-admin-site-deploy-seam (2026-07-14).

bp task stamp <id> <worker> <epoch> --criterion N treats N as a 0-BASED index into acceptance_criteria. But bp task get, the rubric, the spawn prompts, and every board render criteria as 1..N. A builder who follows the visible numbering therefore attaches EVERY evidence string to the criterion one slot LATER than intended.

Why it is worse than a cosmetic off-by-one: on a 7-criterion task whose #7 is the standard '[MERGE-GATED — the lead closes this]' criterion, a builder stamping 1..6 flips criteria 2..7 — which MARKS THE MERGE-GATED CRITERION MET before the PR even exists. The builder contract explicitly forbids that, and the ledger is what the lead trusts at merge. It also means five criteria carry evidence that does not describe them, which is exactly the false-done fabrication class the ledger exists to prevent.

I only caught it by dumping evidence-vs-criterion pairs after stamping; nothing in the CLI's output hints at it (each stamp returns a bare 'epoch=N rev=...'). --miss cannot un-flip a lock, so recovery needs a raw bp doc patch of the whole acceptance_criteria array + re-publish.

FIX (pick one, do not do both silently): (a) make --criterion 1-based to match every surface — the least-surprise option, but it is a breaking change for any script already passing 0-based; or (b) keep 0-based and make the CLI ECHO what it stamped ('criterion 3/7: "<first 60 chars>" -> met') so a mis-index is visible in one line. (b) is worth doing REGARDLESS of (a): a stamp that does not name what it stamped cannot be audited.

Guard: refuse --met on a criterion whose text contains 'MERGE-GATED' unless an explicit --merge-gated override is passed. That is a cheap tripwire on the one flip that actually corrupts a lead's merge decision.
Current state
Ready to begin
This task is open and has not yet recorded completion evidence.
Definition of done
bp task stamp --criterion N is unambiguous: either 1-based to match every rendering surface, or documented 0-based AND the CLI echoes the criterion text it stamped so a mis-index is visible immediately.
A regression test proves that stamping the criteria a builder SEES (1..N) lands each evidence string on the criterion it describes.
--met on a criterion whose text contains MERGE-GATED is refused without an explicit override, so a builder cannot pre-flip the leads merge gate.

Why it is worse than a cosmetic off-by-one: on a 7-criterion task whose #7 is the standard '[MERGE-GATED — the lead closes this]' criterion, a builder stamping 1..6 flips criteria 2..7 — which MARKS THE MERGE-GATED CRITERION MET before the PR even exists. The builder contract explicitly forbids that, and the ledger is what the lead trusts at merge. It also means five criteria carry evidence that does not describe them, which is exactly the false-done fabrication class the ledger exists to prevent.

I only caught it by dumping evidence-vs-criterion pairs after stamping; nothing in the CLI's output hints at it (each stamp returns a bare 'epoch=N rev=...'). --miss cannot un-flip a lock, so recovery needs a raw bp doc patch of the whole acceptance_criteria array + re-publish.

FIX (pick one, do not do both silently): (a) make --criterion 1-based to match every surface — the least-surprise option, but it is a breaking change for any script already passing 0-based; or (b) keep 0-based and make the CLI ECHO what it stamped ('criterion 3/7: "<first 60 chars>" -> met') so a mis-index is visible in one line. (b) is worth doing REGARDLESS of (a): a stamp that does not name what it stamped cannot be audited.

Guard: refuse --met on a criterion whose text contains 'MERGE-GATED' unless an explicit --merge-gated override is passed. That is a cheap tripwire on the one flip that actually corrupts a lead's merge decision.

source.description: The /new ready screen hands off to vercel.com/new/clone, whose form can only prefill env NAMES — the user must paste all 6 values (BARKPARK_API_URL/TOKEN/WORKSPACE/PROJECT/DATASET/WEBHOOK_SECRET) by hand, and values can never ride the URL (TOKEN + WEBHOOK_SECRET are secrets). Replace with Vercel's Claim Deployments platform flow: after bootstrap, the control plane deploys the template via the Vercel API with ALL env values already set (POST /files + POST /deployments, or repo-linked), mints a transfer code (POST /projects/:id/transfer-request, 24h validity), and the ready screen shows a 'Claim this deployment' button (vercel.com/claim-deployment?code=...&returnUrl=...). User clicks, picks their team, receives the fully configured live project — zero pasting. Keep the existing /new/clone button as fallback when the platform token is absent (503 feature_not_configured pattern, mirroring the GitHub App seam). HUMAN GATE: a Vercel access token for the control plane account must be created and wired into cloud/.env + compose passthrough before this activates. Interim quick win (optional first slice): per-value copy buttons on the ready screen's env block so each Vercel field is one click.

source.description: Deferred UI slice from ag-studio-capability-hide — the visual layer only; enforcement + access-drop-at-expiry already hold in the parent (@caps map, default-deny event gate, :access_expiry_tick, :access_grants assign). ENDGAME-WAVE SHAPE (charter decision 6, .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md): build access_panel/1 as a sibling FUNCTION component (NOT a LiveComponent — parent-process assigns, same law as airdrop_sheet) in api/lib/barkpark_web/components/studio_components/modals.ex, on the bp kit (Controls). Two honest sections: (1) YOUR ACCESS — the caller's own inbound grants from the existing :access_grants assign, each with scope + capabilities + a live expiry countdown chip; (2) ACTIVE GRANTS IN THIS WORKSPACE — Access.list_grants_for_workspace/1 (workspace view, membership-gated exactly like AccessController.index gates on Auth.authorize :read), each row with grantee, scope, expiry chip, and a one-click Revoke via Access.revoke/2 (idempotent, server-authorized grantor-or-admin). ZERO new query paths — only list_grants_for_workspace, :access_grants, Access.revoke. Events: access-open/access-close MUST join Caps.@safe_events (:none) or the comprehensiveness test trips them as :deny; access-revoke classifies :write (goes through the Caps gate; Access.revoke re-authorizes server-side regardless). Countdown = client-side JS hook on data-expires-at in api/assets/ (per-second visual only; no server timer — the server tick already drops access). A row whose clock hits zero VANISHES on next re-list because active_where excludes it: the panel is a live-active view, not a history log (accepted). DO NOT touch shares_modal (P6 network shares) or item_share_popover (/s/ links) — different features. Wire an entry affordance near the airdrop button (components.ex) gated so grantees see the panel too (their Your-access section). Files: modals.ex, new handlers/access_panel.ex (sibling to handlers/airdrop.ex), components.ex render+trigger, studio_live.ex handler wiring ONLY (do NOT touch the load_access_grants/:access_expiry_tick region at studio_live.ex:97-184 — the ag-liveview-read-liveness slice owns it), caps.ex @safe_events, assets JS. Hard laws: .ex/.heex waits for the Elixir Test CI gate; worktree from origin/main after git fetch; claim first; PR body carries Task: ag-studio-access-panel-countdown. Local gate: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark_web/live/studio/ (run where _build/test is warm — build-borrow into fresh worktrees is broken).

   - AC4 audit→SIEM: cite audit_test.exs + audit/export_test.exs + the new era-w8-audit-auth-events coverage.
   - AC5 trust surface: cite the four real papers (soc2-controls-mapping, VDP, dpa-template, support-tiers) + GDPR/status/backup-DR children; SPLIT human legs → cite backlog era-hg-pen-test, era-hg-dpa-legal-signoff, era-hg-soc2-type2-window.
   - AC6 zero-tax: reword to the two behavioral legs; cite era-w8-zero-tax-harness.
2. Annotate the 3 defensible-unmet children by backfilling their criterion evidence with pointers: era-w3-sso-spike (0/3 → 'superseded by era-w3-saml/oidc-rp/jit-domain'), era-w2-mfa-policy (3/4 → '4th criterion split to era-w2-org-require-mfa, done 4/4'), era-w6-soc2 (2/3 → 'pen test is an honestly-labeled procurement gate, tracked as era-hg-pen-test').

source.description:
DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH RESIDUAL of the airdrop-grants epic (charter D12/D19) — explicitly NOT a confirmed leak, NOT part of the deny-matrix findings, NOT blocking epic closure. Filed standalone so the closed epic keeps zero open children.

Barkpark.Access.broadcast_revoked/1 (api/lib/barkpark/access.ex:559-565) publishes {:airdrop_revoked} on user:#{grantee_user_id} only when the revoked grant has a bound grantee_user_id (when is_binary(uid) guard). An UNCLAIMED grant (no bound user) revokes silently — broadcast_revoked(_grant), do: :ok.

Verified inert on merged main (post #2177/#2145), stronger than the original charter phrasing:
- Only a CLAIMED grant has a bound grantee_user_id (claiming requires an authenticated User — access.ex:204 claim/2 sets grantee_user_id + claimed_at atomically). There is no token-grantee or anonymous-grantee concept in the Grant schema — grants bind exclusively to a User id.
- StudioLive.mount/3 (live/studio/studio_live.ex:71-79) subscribes to user:#{uid} ONLY for socket.assigns[:current_user] matching %{id: uid} when is_binary(uid) — token-only and anonymous Studio sockets never subscribe, so they can never miss a revoke signal they were never eligible to receive.
- Token and anonymous CallerContexts NEVER CARRY GRANTS AT ALL (caller_context.ex from_token/1 line 49 and anonymous/0 line 42 never invoke resolve_grants; only from_user/2 does) — structurally nothing to go stale for those principals.
- Authenticated-User HTTP reads rebuild CallerContext fresh every request (require_user_session.ex:57 -> CallerContext.from_user -> Access.list_active_grants_for_grantee, active/not-revoked/not-expired/not-spent filtered in-query) — a revoke is visible on the very next HTTP request regardless of this function.

The only theoretical exposure is a FUTURE surface that mounts a live (LiveView/socket) session keyed to an UNCLAIMED grant (e.g. a pre-claim preview desk). No such surface exists today. Parked deliberately; do not build without one.
source.title: broadcast_revoked/1 has zero LiveView blast radius for unbound-grant sockets — defense-in-depth residual, NOT a confirmed leak

Purpose
The heatmap O(1) path engages only above @heatmap_threshold 300 (room.ex:58) and set_heatmap_threshold/2 has NO production call path: zero HTTP/channel/LiveView callers, and guerrilla runs a non-distributed BEAM (mix phx.server from source; no epmd/-sname/release console) — box-level proven 2026-07-12. hq-w1-live-verify therefore parks the heatmap leg as decoder-only (Decision J). Two honest options: (a) an admin-gated verb (HTTP or channel, admin token required) that calls Quiz.set_heatmap_threshold/2 — new .ex code, own PR through the Elixir Test gate, use-and-document; (b) a scripted load harness opening >300 real WS connections to wss://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/quiz/websocket joining one room (the wire protocol is proven at N=1 by the 2026-07-12 synthetic probe: Phoenix V2 join + binary cursors frames, 2+6N codec) — heavier and rate-limit-unverified at scale. Either way the proof is a live 2048-byte heatmap frame + the purple density cloud on the host canvas, then teardown (threshold restored / connections closed; rooms self-reap).
Current state
Ready to begin
This task is open and has not yet recorded completion evidence.
Definition of done
A live heatmap frame (constant 2048B) observed on guerrilla and the host canvas renders the density cloud; evidence recorded (frames + screenshot)
Whatever lever was used is reversible and reversed: threshold restored to 300 / harness connections closed; teardown evidence recorded
